2.23.m: Until teeth appear, [purification is] immediate for a uterine brother; until the tonsure rite, it lasts one night; / until marriage, it lasts three nights; beyond that, ten nights.

2.23.s:
mātāmahānāṃ maraṇe trirātraṃ syādaśaucakam /
ekodakānāṃ maraṇe sūtake caitadeva hi //
2.23.d:
मातामहानां मरणे त्रिरात्रं स्यादशौचकम् ।
एकोदकानां मरणे सूतके चैतदेव हि ॥
2.23.m: On the death of maternal grandfathers, impurity lasts three nights; / and this very same [rule applies] on the death or birth of relatives connected by libations of water.

2.23.s:
pakṣiṇī yonisambandhe bāndhaveṣu tathaiva ca /
ekarātraṃ samuddiṣṭaṃ gurau sabrahmacāriṇi //
2.23.d:
पक्षिणी योनिसम्बन्धे बान्धवेषु तथैव च ।
एकरात्रं समुद्दिष्टं गुरौ सब्रह्मचारिणि ॥
2.23.m: A day and a half is prescribed for blood relatives, and likewise for uterine kin; / one night is enjoined for a guru or a fellow Vedic student.

2.23.s:
prete rājani sajyotiryasya syād viṣaye sthitiḥ /
gṛhe mṛtāsu dattāsu kanyakāsu tryahaṃ pituḥ //
2.23.d:
प्रेते राजनि सज्योतिर्यस्य स्याद् विषये स्थितिः ।
गृहे मृतासु दत्तासु कन्यकासु त्र्यहं पितुः ॥
2.23.m: When a king dies, [impurity lasts] as long as the day or night endures for one living in his realm; / when married daughters die in the [paternal] house, [impurity lasts] three days for the father.

2.23.s:
parapūrvāsu bhāryāsu putreṣu kṛtakeṣu ca /
trirātraṃ syāt tathācārye svabhāryāsvanyagāsu ca //
2.23.d:
परपूर्वासु भार्यासु पुत्रेषु कृतकेषु च ।
त्रिरात्रं स्यात् तथाचार्ये स्वभार्यास्वन्यगासु च ॥
2.23.m: For wives previously married to another, for adopted sons, / and likewise for an ācārya and one's own wives who have gone to another, it lasts three nights.

2.23.s:
ācāryaputre patnyāṃ ca ahorātramudāhṛtam /
ekāhaṃ syādupādhyāye svagrāme śrotriye 'pi ca //
2.23.d:
आचार्यपुत्रे पत्न्यां च अहोरात्रमुदाहृतम् ।
एकाहं स्यादुपाध्याये स्वग्रामे श्रोत्रिये ऽपि च ॥
2.23.m: For the son of an ācārya and for his wife, a day and a night is declared; / it lasts one day for an upādhyāya, and also for a Vedic scholar in one's own village.

2.23.s:
trirātramasapiṇḍeṣu svagṛhe saṃsthiteṣu ca /
ekāhaṃ cāsvavarye syādekarātraṃ tadiṣyate //
2.23.d:
त्रिरात्रमसपिण्डेषु स्वगृहे संस्थितेषु च ।
एकाहं चास्ववर्ये स्यादेकरात्रं तदिष्यते ॥
2.23.m: [It lasts] three nights for non-sapiṇḍas who die in one's own house; / and it lasts one day for one of a different caste, or one night is prescribed.

2.23.s:
trirātraṃ śvaśrūmaraṇe śvaśure vai tadeva hi /
sadyaḥ śaucaṃ samuddiṣṭaṃ sagotre saṃsthite sati //
2.23.d:
त्रिरात्रं श्वश्रूमरणे श्वशुरे वै तदेव हि ।
सद्यः शौचं समुद्दिष्टं सगोत्रे संस्थिते सति ॥
2.23.m: On the death of a mother-in-law, it lasts three nights, and indeed the same for a father-in-law; / immediate purification is enjoined when a member of the same gotra dies.

2.23.s:
śuddhyed vipro daśāhena dvādaśāhena bhūmipaḥ /
vaiśyaḥ pañcadaśāhena śūdro māsena śudyati //
2.23.d:
शुद्ध्येद् विप्रो दशाहेन द्वादशाहेन भूमिपः ।
वैश्यः पञ्चदशाहेन शूद्रो मासेन शुद्यति ॥
2.23.m: A Brāhmaṇa is purified in ten days, a king in twelve days, / a Vaiśya in fifteen days, and a Śūdra is purified in a month.

2.23.s:
kṣatraviṭśūdradāyādā ye syurviprasya bāndhavāḥ /
teṣāmaśauce viprasya daśāhācchuddhiriṣyate //
2.23.d:
क्षत्रविट्शूद्रदायादा ये स्युर्विप्रस्य बान्धवाः ।
तेषामशौचे विप्रस्य दशाहाच्छुद्धिरिष्यते ॥
2.23.m: Those who are heirs belonging to the Kṣatriya, Vaiśya, or Śūdra classes, and are kin of a Brāhmaṇa— / in the impurity of those, purification for the Brāhmaṇa is prescribed after ten days.

2.23.s:
rājanyavaiśyāvapyevaṃ hīnavarṇāsu yoniṣu /
svameva śaucaṃ kuryātāṃ viśuddhyarthamasaṃśayam //
2.23.d:
राजन्यवैश्यावप्येवं हीनवर्णासु योनिषु ।
स्वमेव शौचं कुर्यातां विशुद्ध्यर्थमसंशयम् ॥
2.23.m: Likewise, a Kṣatriya and a Vaiśya, in the case of relations of lower caste, / should observe their own period of purity for purification, without doubt.

2.23.s:
sarve tūttaravarṇānāmaśaucaṃ kuryurādṛtāḥ /
tadvarṇavidhidṛṣṭena svaṃ tu śaucaṃ svayoniṣu //
2.23.d:
सर्वे तूत्तरवर्णानामशौचं कुर्युरादृताः ।
तद्वर्णविधिदृष्टेन स्वं तु शौचं स्वयोनिषु ॥
2.23.m: All persons, however, should observe the impurity of the higher castes with respect, / according to the rule laid down for that caste, but their own period of purity among their own kind.

2.23.s:
ṣaḍrātraṃ vā trirātraṃ syādekarātraṃ krameṇa hi /
vaiśyakṣatriyaviprāṇāṃ śūdreṣvāśaucameva tu //
2.23.d:
षड्रात्रं वा त्रिरात्रं स्यादेकरात्रं क्रमेण हि ।
वैश्यक्षत्रियविप्राणां शूद्रेष्वाशौचमेव तु ॥
2.23.m: Six nights, three nights, or one night in order / is indeed the impurity for Vaiśyas, Kṣatriyas, and Brāhmaṇas in the case of Śūdras.

2.23.s:
ardhamāso 'tha ṣaḍrātraṃ trirātraṃ dvijapuṅgavāḥ /
śūdrakṣatriyaviprāṇāṃ vaiśyeṣvāśaucamiṣyate //
2.23.d:
अर्धमासो ऽथ षड्रात्रं त्रिरात्रं द्विजपुङ्गवाः ।
शूद्रक्षत्रियविप्राणां वैश्येष्वाशौचमिष्यते ॥
2.23.m: Half a month, six nights, and three nights, O best of the twice-born, / is the impurity prescribed for Śūdras, Kṣatriyas, and Brāhmaṇas in the case of Vaiśyas.

2.23.s:
ṣaḍrātraṃ vai daśāhaṃ ca viprāṇāṃ vaiśyaśūdrayoḥ /
aśaucaṃ kṣatriye proktaṃ krameṇa dvijapuṅgavāḥ //
2.23.d:
षड्रात्रं वै दशाहं च विप्राणां वैश्यशूद्रयोः ।
अशौचं क्षत्रिये प्रोक्तं क्रमेण द्विजपुङ्गवाः ॥
2.23.m: Six nights and ten days for Brāhmaṇas, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras, / in order, O best of the twice-born, is declared to be the impurity in the case of a Kṣatriya.

2.23.s:
śūdraviṭkṣatriyāṇāṃ tu brāhmaṇe saṃsthite sati /
daśarātreṇa śuddhiḥ syādityāha kamalodbhavaḥ //
2.23.d:
शूद्रविट्क्षत्रियाणां तु ब्राह्मणे संस्थिते सति ।
दशरात्रेण शुद्धिः स्यादित्याह कमलोद्भवः ॥
2.23.m: When a Brāhmaṇa dies, for Śūdras, Vaiśyas, and Kṣatriyas, / purification occurs in ten nights; so said the Lotus-born [Brahmā].

2.23.s:
asapiṇḍaṃ dvijaṃ pretaṃ vipro nirhṛtya bandhuvat /
aśitvā ca sahoṣitvā daśarātreṇa śudhyati //
2.23.d:
असपिण्डं द्विजं प्रेतं विप्रो निर्हृत्य बन्धुवत् ।
अशित्वा च सहोषित्वा दशरात्रेण शुध्यति ॥
2.23.m: A Brāhmaṇa who carries out a deceased twice-born non-sapiṇḍa like a kinsman, / eating with them and staying with them, is purified in ten nights.

2.23.s:
yadyannamatti teṣāṃ tu trirātreṇa tataḥ śuciḥ /
anadannannamahnaiva na ca tasmin gṛhe vaset //
2.23.d:
यद्यन्नमत्ति तेषां तु त्रिरात्रेण ततः शुचिः ।
अनदन्नन्नमह्नैव न च तस्मिन् गृहे वसेत् ॥
2.23.m: If he eats their food, he becomes pure after three nights; / not eating their food and not dwelling in that house, [he is pure] in just one day.

2.23.s:
sodakeṣvetadeva syānmāturāpteṣu bandhuṣu /
daśāhena śavasparśe sapiṇḍaścaiva śudhyati //
2.23.d:
सोदकेष्वेतदेव स्यान्मातुराप्तेषु बन्धुषु ।
दशाहेन शवस्पर्शे सपिण्डश्चैव शुध्यति ॥
2.23.m: The same rule applies in the case of water-kinsmen and close relatives of the mother; / and upon touching a corpse, a sapiṇḍa is purified in ten days.

2.23.s:
yadi nirharati pretaṃ prolabhākrāntamānasaḥ /
daśāhena dvijaḥ śudhyed dvādaśāhena bhūmipaḥ //
2.23.d:
यदि निर्हरति प्रेतं प्रोलभाक्रान्तमानसः ।
दशाहेन द्विजः शुध्येद् द्वादशाहेन भूमिपः ॥
2.23.m: If one carries out a deceased person with a mind overcome by greed, / a twice-born is purified in ten days, and a king in twelve days.

2.23.s:
ardhamāsena vaiśyastu śūdro māsena śudhyati /
ṣaḍrātreṇāthavā sarve trirātreṇāthavā punaḥ //
2.23.d:
अर्धमासेन वैश्यस्तु शूद्रो मासेन शुध्यति ।
षड्रात्रेणाथवा सर्वे त्रिरात्रेणाथवा पुनः ॥
2.23.m: A Vaiśya is purified in half a month, and a Śūdra is purified in a month; / or all of them [are purified] in six nights, or again in three nights.

2.23.s:
anāthaṃ caiva nirhṛtya brāhmaṇaṃ dhanavarjitam /
snātvā saṃprāśya tu ghṛtaṃ śudhyanti brāhmaṇādayaḥ //
2.23.d:
अनाथं चैव निर्हृत्य ब्राह्मणं धनवर्जितम् ।
स्नात्वा संप्राश्य तु घृतं शुध्यन्ति ब्राह्मणादयः ॥
2.23.m: Having carried out a destitute Brāhmaṇa who was without a protector, / Brāhmaṇas and others are purified after bathing and tasting clarified butter.

2.23.s:
avaraśced varaṃ varṇamavaraṃ vā varo yadi /
aśauce saṃspṛśet snehāt tadāśaucena śudhyati //
2.23.d:
अवरश्चेद् वरं वर्णमवरं वा वरो यदि ।
अशौचे संस्पृशेत् स्नेहात् तदाशौचेन शुध्यति ॥
2.23.m: If a lower caste person touches a higher caste person, or a higher caste touches a lower / during impurity out of affection, he is purified according to that person's impurity.

2.23.s:
pretībhūtaṃ dvijaṃ vipro yo 'nugacchata kāmataḥ /
snātvā sacailaṃ spṛṣṭvāgniṃ ghṛtaṃ prāśya viśudhyati //
2.23.d:
प्रेतीभूतं द्विजं विप्रो यो ऽनुगच्छत कामतः ।
स्नात्वा सचैलं स्पृष्ट्वाग्निं घृतं प्राश्य विशुध्यति ॥
2.23.m: A Brāhmaṇa who intentionally follows a deceased twice-born person / becomes pure after bathing with his clothes on, touching fire, and tasting clarified butter.

2.23.s:
ekāhāt kṣatriye śuddhirvaiśye syācca dvyahena tu /
śūdre dinatrayaṃ proktaṃ prāṇāyāmaśataṃ punaḥ //
2.23.d:
एकाहात् क्षत्रिये शुद्धिर्वैश्ये स्याच्च द्व्यहेन तु ।
शूद्रे दिनत्रयं प्रोक्तं प्राणायामशतं पुनः ॥
2.23.m: Purification occurs after one day in the case of a Kṣatriya, after two days in the case of a Vaiśya; / three days are declared in the case of a Śūdra, along with a hundred breath controls.

2.23.s:
anasthisaṃcite śūdre rauti ced brāhmaṇaḥ svakaiḥ /
trirātraṃ syāt tathāśaucamekāhaṃ tvanyathā smṛtam //
2.23.d:
अनस्थिसंचिते शूद्रे रौति चेद् ब्राह्मणः स्वकैः ।
त्रिरात्रं स्यात् तथाशौचमेकाहं त्वन्यथा स्मृतम् ॥
2.23.m: If a Brāhmaṇa weeps along with the relatives over a Śūdra whose bones have not been gathered, / the impurity lasts three nights; otherwise, it is remembered as lasting one day.

2.23.s:
asthisaṃcayanādarvāgekāhaṃ kṣatravaiśyayoḥ /
anyathā caiva sajyotirbrāhmaṇe snānameva tu //
2.23.d:
अस्थिसंचयनादर्वागेकाहं क्षत्रवैश्ययोः ।
अन्यथा चैव सज्योतिर्ब्राह्मणे स्नानमेव तु ॥
2.23.m: Before the collection of the bones, [impurity lasts] one day for a Kṣatriya and a Vaiśya; / otherwise, it is until the appearance of stars, but in the case of a Brāhmaṇa, bathing alone [is required].

2.23.s:
anasthisaṃcit vipre brāhmaṇo rauti cet tadā /
snānenaiva bhavecchuddhiḥ sacailena na saṃśayaḥ //
2.23.d:
अनस्थिसंचित् विप्रे ब्राह्मणो रौति चेत् तदा ।
स्नानेनैव भवेच्छुद्धिः सचैलेन न संशयः ॥
2.23.m: If a Brāhmaṇa weeps for a Brāhmaṇa whose bones have not been collected, / then purification occurs merely through bathing with one's clothes on, there is no doubt.

2.23.s:
yastaiḥ sahāśanaṃ kuryācchayanādīni caiva hi /
bāndhavo vāparo vāpi sa daśāhena śudhyati //
2.23.d:
यस्तैः सहाशनं कुर्याच्छयनादीनि चैव हि ।
बान्धवो वापरो वापि स दशाहेन शुध्यति ॥
2.23.m: Whoever shares a meal or takes rest with them, / whether a relative or another person, becomes purified after ten days.

2.23.s:
yasteṣāmannamaśnāti sakṛdevāpi kāmataḥ /
tadāśauce nivṛtte 'sau snānaṃ kṛtvā viśudhyati //
2.23.d:
यस्तेषामन्नमश्नाति सकृदेवापि कामतः ।
तदाशौचे निवृत्ते ऽसौ स्नानं कृत्वा विशुध्यति ॥
2.23.m: Whoever eats their food even once intentionally, / becomes purified by taking a bath once that period of impurity has ended.

2.23.s:
yāvattadannamaśnāti durbhikṣopahato naraḥ /
tāvantyahānyaśaucaṃ syāt prāyaścittaṃ tataścaret //
2.23.d:
यावत्तदन्नमश्नाति दुर्भिक्षोपहतो नरः ।
तावन्त्यहान्यशौचं स्यात् प्रायश्चित्तं ततश्चरेत् ॥
2.23.m: For as many days as a man, struck by famine, eats their food, / for that many days there shall be impurity, and he should then perform an expiation.

2.23.s:
dāhādyaśaucaṃ kartavyaṃ dvijānāmagnihotriṇām /
sapiṇḍānāṃ tu maraṇe maraṇāditareṣu ca //
2.23.d:
दाहाद्यशौचं कर्तव्यं द्विजानामग्निहोत्रिणाम् ।
सपिण्डानां तु मरणे मरणादितरेषु च ॥
2.23.m: Impurity should be observed from the time of cremation for twice-born maintainers of the sacred fire, / but upon the death of sapiṇḍas, and for others, [it begins] from the moment of death.

2.23.s:
sapiṇḍatā ca puruṣe saptame vinivartate /
samānodakabhāvastu janmanāmnoravedane //
2.23.d:
सपिण्डता च पुरुषे सप्तमे विनिवर्तते ।
समानोदकभावस्तु जन्मनाम्नोरवेदने ॥
2.23.m: The status of being sapiṇḍas ceases in the seventh generation, / but the relationship of samānodakas ceases when birth and names are no longer remembered.

2.23.s:
pitā pitāmahaścaiva tathaiva prapitāmahaḥ /
lepabhājastrayaścātmā sāpiṇḍyaṃ sāptapauruṣaṇ //
2.23.d:
पिता पितामहश्चैव तथैव प्रपितामहः ।
लेपभाजस्त्रयश्चात्मा सापिण्ड्यं साप्तपौरुषण् ॥
2.23.m: The father, the grandfather, and likewise the great-grandfather, / three sharers of the oblation-wipings, and oneself—the status of sapiṇḍa extends through seven generations.

2.23.s:
aprattānāṃ tathā strīṇāṃ sāpiṇḍyaṃ sāptapauruṣam /
ūḍhānāṃ bhartusāpiṇḍyaṃ prāha devaḥ pitāmahaḥ //
2.23.d:
अप्रत्तानां तथा स्त्रीणां सापिण्ड्यं साप्तपौरुषम् ।
ऊढानां भर्तुसापिण्ड्यं प्राह देवः पितामहः ॥
2.23.m: For unmarried women, the sapiṇḍa relationship extends through seven generations; / for married women, the sapiṇḍa relationship is with the husband: thus spoke the divine Grandfather.

2.23.s:
ye caikajātā bahavo bhinnayonaya eva ca /
bhinnavarṇāstu sāpiṇḍyaṃ bhavet teṣāṃ tripūruṣam //
2.23.d:
ये चैकजाता बहवो भिन्नयोनय एव च ।
भिन्नवर्णास्तु सापिण्ड्यं भवेत् तेषां त्रिपूरुषम् ॥
2.23.m: And those born of one father but different wombs, / being of different castes, their sapiṇḍa relationship extends to three generations.

2.23.s:
kāravaḥ śilpino vaidyā dāsīdāsāstathaiva ca /
dātāro niyamī caiva brahmavidbrahmacāriṇau //
2.23.d:
कारवः शिल्पिनो वैद्या दासीदासास्तथैव च ।
दातारो नियमी चैव ब्रह्मविद्ब्रह्मचारिणौ ॥
2.23.m: Artisans, craftsmen, physicians, as well as female and male slaves, / generous donors, one bound by an observance, the knower of Brahman, and the student of the Veda,

2.23.s:
satriṇo vratinastāvat sadyaḥ śaucā udāhṛtāḥ /
rājā caivābhiṣiktaśca prāṇasatriṇa eva ca //
2.23.d:
सत्रिणो व्रतिनस्तावत् सद्यः शौचा उदाहृताः ।
राजा चैवाभिषिक्तश्च प्राणसत्रिण एव च ॥
2.23.m: sacrificers, and those undergoing a vow are declared to be purified immediately; / and also an anointed king, and those performing the sacrifice of life.

2.23.s:
yajñe vivāhakāle ca devayāge tathaiva ca /
sadyaḥ śaucaṃ samākhyātaṃ durbhikṣe cāpyupadrave //
2.23.d:
यज्ञे विवाहकाले च देवयागे तथैव च ।
सद्यः शौचं समाख्यातं दुर्भिक्षे चाप्युपद्रवे ॥
2.23.m: In a sacrifice, at the time of marriage, and likewise in a rite for the gods, / immediate purification is proclaimed, as well as during a famine or a calamity.

2.23.s:
ḍimbāhavahatānāṃ ca vidyutā pārthivairdvijaiḥ /
sadyaḥ śaucaṃ samākhyātaṃ sarpādimaraṇe tathā //
2.23.d:
डिम्बाहवहतानां च विद्युता पार्थिवैर्द्विजैः ।
सद्यः शौचं समाख्यातं सर्पादिमरणे तथा ॥
2.23.m: For those killed in riots and battles, by lightning, by kings, or by twice-born men, / immediate purification is proclaimed, and likewise in death caused by a snake and the like.

2.23.s:
agnau maruprapatane vīrādhvanyapyanāśake /
brāhmaṇārthe ca saṃnyaste sadyaḥ śaucaṃ vidhīyate //
2.23.d:
अग्नौ मरुप्रपतने वीराध्वन्यप्यनाशके ।
ब्राह्मणार्थे च संन्यस्ते सद्यः शौचं विधीयते ॥
2.23.m: In entering fire, leaping from a cliff, on the hero's path, in fasting to death, / for the sake of a Brāhmaṇa, or when having renounced, immediate purification is prescribed.

2.23.s:
naiṣṭhikānāṃ vanasthānāṃ yatīnāṃ brahmacāriṇām /
nāśaucaṃ kīrtyate sadbhiḥ patite ca tathā mṛte //
2.23.d:
नैष्ठिकानां वनस्थानां यतीनां ब्रह्मचारिणाम् ।
नाशौचं कीर्त्यते सद्भिः पतिते च तथा मृते ॥
2.23.m: For perpetual students, forest hermits, ascetics, and students of the Veda, / no impurity is declared by the virtuous; and likewise when an outcaste has died.

2.23.s:
patitānāṃ na dāhaḥ syānnāntyeṣṭirnāsthisaṃcayaḥ /
na cāśrupātapiṇḍau vā kāryaṃ śrāddhādi kaṅkvacit //
2.23.d:
पतितानां न दाहः स्यान्नान्त्येष्टिर्नास्थिसंचयः ।
न चाश्रुपातपिण्डौ वा कार्यं श्राद्धादि कङ्क्वचित् ॥
2.23.m: For outcastes there shall be no cremation, no funeral rite, and no collection of bones, / neither the shedding of tears nor funeral cakes, nor should any ancestral offering rite and the like be performed anywhere.

2.23.s:
vyāpādayet tathātmānaṃ svayaṃ yo 'gniviṣādibhiḥ /
vihitaṃ tasya nāśaucaṃ nāgnirnāpyudakādikam //
2.23.d:
व्यापादयेत् तथात्मानं स्वयं यो ऽग्निविषादिभिः ।
विहितं तस्य नाशौचं नाग्निर्नाप्युदकादिकम् ॥
2.23.m: Whoever destroys himself by fire, poison, and the like, / for him no impurity is ordained, neither fire nor water offerings and the like.

2.23.s:
atha kaścit pramādena mriyate 'gniviṣādibhiḥ /
tasyāśaucaṃ vidhātavyaṃ kāryaṃ caivodakādikam //
2.23.d:
अथ कश्चित् प्रमादेन म्रियते ऽग्निविषादिभिः ।
तस्याशौचं विधातव्यं कार्यं चैवोदकादिकम् ॥
2.23.m: Now, if someone dies through negligence by fire, poison, and the like, / impurity should be observed for him, and water offerings and the like must be performed.

2.23.s:
jāte kumāre tadahaḥ kāmaṃ kuryāt pratigraham /
hiraṇyadhānyagovāsastilānnaguḍasarpiṣām //
2.23.d:
जाते कुमारे तदहः कामं कुर्यात् प्रतिग्रहम् ।
हिरण्यधान्यगोवासस्तिलान्नगुडसर्पिषाम् ॥
2.23.m: When a son is born, on that day one may freely accept gifts / of gold, grain, cattle, clothing, sesame, cooked food, molasses, and clarified butter.

2.23.s:
phalāni puṣpaṃ śākaṃ ca lavaṇaṃ kāṣṭhameva ca /
toyaṃ dadhi ghṛtaṃ tailamauṣadhaṃ kṣīrameva ca /
āśaucināṃ gṛhād grāhyaṃ śuṣkānnaṃ caiva nityaśaḥ //
2.23.d:
फलानि पुष्पं शाकं च लवणं काष्ठमेव च ।
तोयं दधि घृतं तैलमौषधं क्षीरमेव च ।
आशौचिनां गृहाद् ग्राह्यं शुष्कान्नं चैव नित्यशः ॥
2.23.m: Fruits, flowers, vegetables, salt, firewood, / water, curd, clarified butter, oil, medicine, and milk, / and dry food may always be accepted from the house of those who are impure.

2.23.s:
āhitāgniryathānyāyaṃ dagdhavyastribhiragnibhiḥ /
anāhitāgnirgṛhyeṇa laukikenetaro janaḥ //
2.23.d:
आहिताग्निर्यथान्यायं दग्धव्यस्त्रिभिरग्निभिः ।
अनाहिताग्निर्गृह्येण लौकिकेनेतरो जनः ॥
2.23.m: One who maintains the sacred fires should be cremated with the three fires according to rule; / one who does not maintain the sacred fires with the domestic fire, and other people with the common fire.

2.23.s:
dehābhāvāt palāśaistu kṛtvā pratikṛtiṃ punaḥ /
dāhaḥ kāryo yathānyāyaṃ sapiṇḍaiḥ śraddhayānvitaiḥ //
2.23.d:
देहाभावात् पलाशैस्तु कृत्वा प्रतिकृतिं पुनः ।
दाहः कार्यो यथान्यायं सपिण्डैः श्रद्धयान्वितैः ॥
2.23.m: In the absence of a body, however, having made an effigy out of palāśa leaves, / cremation should be performed according to rule by the sapiṇḍas endowed with faith.

2.23.s:
sakṛtprasiñcantyudakaṃ nāmagotreṇa vāgyatāḥ /
daśāhaṃ bāndhavaiḥ sārdhaṃ sarve caivārdravāsasaḥ //
2.23.d:
सकृत्प्रसिञ्चन्त्युदकं नामगोत्रेण वाग्यताः ।
दशाहं बान्धवैः सार्धं सर्वे चैवार्द्रवाससः ॥
2.23.m: With restrained speech, wearing wet clothes together with the kinsmen, / they should pour water once, uttering the name and lineage, for ten days.

2.23.s:
piṇḍaṃ pratidinaṃ dadyuḥ sāyaṃ prātaryathāvidhi /
pretāya ca gṛhadvāri caturthe bhojayed dvijān //
2.23.d:
पिण्डं प्रतिदिनं दद्युः सायं प्रातर्यथाविधि ।
प्रेताय च गृहद्वारि चतुर्थे भोजयेद् द्विजान् ॥
2.23.m: They should offer a funeral cake every day at evening and morning according to the rule, / for the deceased spirit at the door of the house, and on the fourth day feed the twice-born.

2.23.s:
dvitīye 'hani kartavyaṃ kṣurakarma sabāndhavaiḥ /
caturthe bāndhavaiḥ sarvairasthanāṃ saṃcayanaṃ bhavet /
pūrvaṃ tu bhojayed viprānayugmān śraddhayā śucīn //
2.23.d:
द्वितीये ऽहनि कर्तव्यं क्षुरकर्म सबान्धवैः ।
चतुर्थे बान्धवैः सर्वैरस्थनां संचयनं भवेत् ।
पूर्वं तु भोजयेद् विप्रानयुग्मान् श्रद्धया शुचीन् ॥
2.23.m: On the second day, shaving should be performed together with the relatives; / on the fourth day, the collection of bones should be performed by all the relatives; / but first, one should feed pure twice-born men in odd numbers with faith.

2.23.s:
pañcame navame caiva tathaivaikādaśe 'hani /
ayugmān bhojayed viprān navaśrāddhaṃ tu tadviduḥ //
2.23.d:
पञ्चमे नवमे चैव तथैवैकादशे ऽहनि ।
अयुग्मान् भोजयेद् विप्रान् नवश्राद्धं तु तद्विदुः ॥
2.23.m: On the fifth, ninth, and likewise eleventh day, / one should feed twice-born men in odd numbers; they know this as the rite for the newly deceased.

2.23.s:
ekādaśe 'hni kurvota pretamuddiśya bhāvataḥ /
dvādaśe vātha kartavyamanindye tvathavāhani /
ekaṃ pavitramekor'ghaḥ piṇḍapātraṃ tathaiva ca //
2.23.d:
एकादशे ऽह्नि कुर्वोत प्रेतमुद्दिश्य भावतः ।
द्वादशे वाथ कर्तव्यमनिन्द्ये त्वथवाहनि ।
एकं पवित्रमेकोर्ऽघः पिण्डपात्रं तथैव च ॥
2.23.m: On the eleventh day, one should perform [the rite] for the deceased spirit with devotion, / or it should be done on the twelfth day, or on an unblamable day; / there should be one strain of darbha grass, one water offering, and likewise one cake vessel.

2.23.s:
evaṃ mṛtāhni kartavyaṃ pratimāsaṃ tu vatsaram /
sapiṇḍīkaraṇaṃ proktaṃ pūrṇe saṃvatsare punaḥ //
2.23.d:
एवं मृताह्नि कर्तव्यं प्रतिमासं तु वत्सरम् ।
सपिण्डीकरणं प्रोक्तं पूर्णे संवत्सरे पुनः ॥
2.23.m: In this manner, it should be done on the day of death each month for a year; / when the year is completed, the sapiṇḍīkaraṇa rite is prescribed once more.

2.23.s:
kuryāccatvāri pātrāṇi pretādīnāṃ dvijottamāḥ /
pretārthaṃ pitṛpātreṣu pātramāsecayet tataḥ //
2.23.d:
कुर्याच्चत्वारि पात्राणि प्रेतादीनां द्विजोत्तमाः ।
प्रेतार्थं पितृपात्रेषु पात्रमासेचयेत् ततः ॥
2.23.m: One should prepare four vessels for the deceased spirit and the ancestors, O best of the twice-born; / then one should pour the vessel for the deceased spirit into the vessels for the ancestors,

2.23.s:
ye samānā iti dvābhyāṃ piṇḍānapyevameva hi /
sapiṇḍīkaraṇaṃ śrāddhaṃ devapūrvaṃ vidhīyate //
2.23.d:
ये समाना इति द्वाभ्यां पिण्डानप्येवमेव हि ।
सपिण्डीकरणं श्राद्धं देवपूर्वं विधीयते ॥
2.23.m: along with the two verses 'ye samānāḥ'; and the funeral cakes in this very same manner; / the sapiṇḍīkaraṇa ancestral offering rite is ordained to be preceded by an offering to the gods.

2.23.s:
pitṝnāvāhayet tatra punaḥ pretaṃ ca nirdiśet /
ye sapiṇḍīkṛtāḥ pretāna teṣāṃ syāt pṛthakkriyāḥ /
yastu kuryāt pṛthak piṇḍaṃ pitṛhā so 'bhijāyate //
2.23.d:
पितॄनावाहयेत् तत्र पुनः प्रेतं च निर्दिशेत् ।
ये सपिण्डीकृताः प्रेतान तेषां स्यात् पृथक्क्रियाः ।
यस्तु कुर्यात् पृथक् पिण्डं पितृहा सो ऽभिजायते ॥
2.23.m: One should invoke the ancestors there, and again designate the deceased spirit; / for those deceased spirits who have been united through the sapiṇḍīkaraṇa rite, there can be no separate rites; / whoever makes a separate cake becomes a killer of his ancestors.

2.23.s:
mṛte pitari vai putraḥ piṇḍamabdaṃ samācaret /
dadyāccānnaṃ sodakumbhaṃ pratyahaṃ pretadharmataḥ //
2.23.d:
मृते पितरि वै पुत्रः पिण्डमब्दं समाचरेत् ।
दद्याच्चान्नं सोदकुम्भं प्रत्यहं प्रेतधर्मतः ॥
2.23.m: When the father dies, the son should indeed perform the offering of the funeral cake for a year, / and give food with a jar of water every day according to the duty toward the deceased spirit.

2.23.s:
pārvaṇena vidhānena saṃvatsarikamiṣyate /
pratisaṃvatsaraṃ kāryaṃ vidhireṣa sanātanaḥ //
2.23.d:
पार्वणेन विधानेन संवत्सरिकमिष्यते ।
प्रतिसंवत्सरं कार्यं विधिरेष सनातनः ॥
2.23.m: The annual rite is prescribed according to the rules of the new-and-full-moon ancestor rites; / it should be performed every year; this is the eternal rule.

2.23.s:
mātāpitroḥ sutaiḥ kāryaṃ piṇḍadānādikaṃ ca yat /
patnī kuryāt sutābhāve patnya bhāve sahodahaḥ //
2.23.d:
मातापित्रोः सुतैः कार्यं पिण्डदानादिकं च यत् ।
पत्नी कुर्यात् सुताभावे पत्न्य भावे सहोदहः ॥
2.23.m: Whatever offering of cakes and the like must be done for parents by sons, / the wife should do in the absence of a son, and a uterine brother in the absence of a wife.

2.23.s:
anenaiva vidhāne jīvan vā śrāddhamācaret /
kṛtvā dānādikaṃ sarvaṃ śraddhāyuktaḥ samāhitaḥ //
2.23.d:
अनेनैव विधाने जीवन् वा श्राद्धमाचरेत् ।
कृत्वा दानादिकं सर्वं श्रद्धायुक्तः समाहितः ॥
2.23.m: According to this very rule, while living, one may perform an ancestral offering rite for oneself, / performing all giving of gifts and the like, endowed with faith and composed in mind.

2.23.s:
eṣa vaḥ kathitaḥ samyag gṛhasthānāṃ kriyāvidhiḥ /
strīṇāṃ tu bhartṛśuśrūṣā dharmo nānya iheṣyate //
2.23.d:
एष वः कथितः सम्यग् गृहस्थानां क्रियाविधिः ।
स्त्रीणां तु भर्तृशुश्रूषा धर्मो नान्य इहेष्यते ॥
2.23.m: This proper rule of rites for householders has been told to you; / for women, however, service to the husband is recognized as duty, none other in this world.

2.23.s:
svadharmaparamo nityamīśvirārpitamānasaḥ /
prāpnoti tat paraṃ sthānaṃ yaduktaṃ vedavādibhiḥ //
iti śrīkūrmapurāṇe ṣaṭsāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāmuparivibhāge trayoviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.23.d:
स्वधर्मपरमो नित्यमीश्विरार्पितमानसः ।
प्राप्नोति तत् परं स्थानं यदुक्तं वेदवादिभिः ॥
इति श्रीकूर्मपुराणे षट्साहस्त्र्यां संहितायामुपरिविभागे त्रयोविंशो ऽध्यायः
2.23.m:
Constantly devoted to his own duty, his mind offered up to the Lord, / he attains that supreme station which is proclaimed by the teachers of the Veda.

Thus ends the twenty-third chapter in the latter section of the compilation of six thousand verses in the glorious Kūrma Purāṇa.

2.24.s:
vyāsa uvāca
agnihotraṃ tu juhuyādādyante 'harniśoḥ sadā /
darśena caiva pakṣānte paurṇamāsena caiva hi //
2.24.d:
व्यास उवाच
अग्निहोत्रं तु जुहुयादाद्यन्ते ऽहर्निशोः सदा ।
दर्शेन चैव पक्षान्ते पौर्णमासेन चैव हि ॥
2.24.m:
Vyāsa said:
One should always offer the agnihotra oblation at the beginning and end of day and night, / and at the end of each fortnight with the new-moon sacrifice and the full-moon sacrifice,

2.24.s:
śasyānte navaśasyeṣṭyā tathartvante dvijo 'dhvaraiḥ /
paśunā tvayanasyānte samānte saumikairmakhaiḥ //
2.24.d:
शस्यान्ते नवशस्येष्ट्या तथर्त्वन्ते द्विजो ऽध्वरैः ।
पशुना त्वयनस्यान्ते समान्ते सौमिकैर्मखैः ॥
2.24.m: at the harvest with the sacrifice of first fruits, and at the end of each season the twice-born should offer with soma sacrifices; / at the end of a half-year with an animal sacrifice, and at the end of the year with soma rites.

2.24.s:
nāniṣṭvā navaśasyeṣṭyā paśunā vāgnimān dvijaḥ /
navānnamadyānmāṃsaṃ vā dīrghamāyurjijīviṣuḥ //
2.24.d:
नानिष्ट्वा नवशस्येष्ट्या पशुना वाग्निमान् द्विजः ।
नवान्नमद्यान्मांसं वा दीर्घमायुर्जिजीविषुः ॥
2.24.m: Without having sacrificed with the offering of first fruits or with an animal, the twice-born maintainer of sacred fire / who wishes to live a long life should not eat new grain or meat.

2.24.s:
navenānnena cāniṣṭvā paśuhavyena cāganyaḥ /
prāṇānevāttumicchanti navānnāmiṣagṛddhinaḥ //
2.24.d:
नवेनान्नेन चानिष्ट्वा पशुहव्येन चागन्यः ।
प्राणानेवात्तुमिच्छन्ति नवान्नामिषगृद्धिनः ॥
2.24.m: When one has not offered the new grain and animal oblations, the sacred fires / wish to consume the very life-breaths of the one who is greedy for new grain and meat.

2.24.s:
sāvitrān śāntihomāṃśca kuryāt parvasu nityaśaḥ /
pitṝṃścaivāṣṭakāsvarcan nityamanvaṣṭakāsu ca //
2.24.d:
सावित्रान् शान्तिहोमांश्च कुर्यात् पर्वसु नित्यशः ।
पितॄंश्चैवाष्टकास्वर्चन् नित्यमन्वष्टकासु च ॥
2.24.m: One should always perform the Sāvitrī oblations and pacificatory fire offerings on the new- and full-moon days, / always worshiping the ancestors on the eighth-day rites and on the days following the eighth.

2.24.s:
eṣa dharmaḥ paro nityamapadharmo 'nya ucyate /
trayāṇāmiha varṇānāṃ gṛhasthāśramavāsinām //
2.24.d:
एष धर्मः परो नित्यमपधर्मो ऽन्य उच्यते ।
त्रयाणामिह वर्णानां गृहस्थाश्रमवासिनाम् ॥
2.24.m: This is the supreme eternal duty; another, the duty in times of distress, is now declared / for the three castes dwelling here in the householder stage of life.

2.24.s:
nāstikyādathavālasyād yo 'gnīn nādhātumicchati /
yajeta vā na yajñena sa yāti narakān bahūn //
2.24.d:
नास्तिक्यादथवालस्याद् यो ऽग्नीन् नाधातुमिच्छति ।
यजेत वा न यज्ञेन स याति नरकान् बहून् ॥
2.24.m:
He who, out of atheism or out of laziness, does not wish to establish the sacred fires
or does not sacrifice with sacrifice, goes to many hells:

2.24.s:
tāmistramandhatāmistraṃ mahārauravarauravau /
kumbhīpākaṃ vaitaraṇīmasipatravanaṃ tathā //
2.24.d:
तामिस्त्रमन्धतामिस्त्रं महारौरवरौरवौ ।
कुम्भीपाकं वैतरणीमसिपत्रवनं तथा ॥
2.24.m:
Tāmistra, Andhatāmistra, Mahāraurava and Raurava,
Kumbhīpāka, Vaitaraṇī, and likewise Asipatravana.

2.24.s:
anyāṃśca narakān ghorān saṃprāpyānte sudurmatiḥ /
antyajānāṃ kule viprāḥ śūdrayonau ca jāyate //
2.24.d:
अन्यांश्च नरकान् घोरान् संप्राप्यान्ते सुदुर्मतिः ।
अन्त्यजानां कुले विप्राः शूद्रयोनौ च जायते ॥
2.24.m:
Having reached other dreadful hells, at the end, that utterly foolish man,
O Brahmins, is born into a family of outcastes and in a Śūdra womb.

2.24.s:
tasmāt sarvaprayatnena brāhmaṇo hi viśeṣataḥ /
ādhāyāgniṃ viśuddhātmā yajeta parameśvaram //
2.24.d:
तस्मात् सर्वप्रयत्नेन ब्राह्मणो हि विशेषतः ।
आधायाग्निं विशुद्धात्मा यजेत परमेश्वरम् ॥
2.24.m:
Therefore, by every effort, a Brahmin especially,
having established the sacred fire with a purified self, should worship the Supreme Lord.

2.24.s:
agnihotrāt paro dharmo dvijānāṃ neha vidyate /
tasmādārādhayennityamagnihotreṇa śāśvatam //
2.24.d:
अग्निहोत्रात् परो धर्मो द्विजानां नेह विद्यते ।
तस्मादाराधयेन्नित्यमग्निहोत्रेण शाश्वतम् ॥
2.24.m:
No duty higher than the Agnihotra exists here for the twice-born;
therefore, one should constantly worship the eternal [Lord] through the Agnihotra.

2.24.s:
yaścādhāyāgnimālasyānna yaṣṭuṃ devamicchati /
so 'sau mūḍho na saṃbhāṣyaḥ kiṃ punarnāstiko janaḥ //
2.24.d:
यश्चाधायाग्निमालस्यान्न यष्टुं देवमिच्छति ।
सो ऽसौ मूढो न संभाष्यः किं पुनर्नास्तिको जनः ॥
2.24.m:
And he who, having established the sacred fire, does not wish to sacrifice to the deity out of laziness,
that foolish man is not to be spoken to; how much less an atheistic person!

2.24.s:
yasya traivārṣikaṃ bhaktaṃ paryāptaṃ bhṛtyavṛttaye /
adhikaṃ cāpi vidyeta sa somaṃ pātumarhati //
2.24.d:
यस्य त्रैवार्षिकं भक्तं पर्याप्तं भृत्यवृत्तये ।
अधिकं चापि विद्येत स सोमं पातुमर्हति ॥
2.24.m:
He who has grain enough for three years to maintain his dependents,
and has even more, is entitled to drink Soma.

2.24.s:
eṣa vai sarvayajñānāṃ somaḥ prathama iṣyate /
somenārādhayed devaṃ somalokamaheśvaram //
2.24.d:
एष वै सर्वयज्ञानां सोमः प्रथम इष्यते ।
सोमेनाराधयेद् देवं सोमलोकमहेश्वरम् ॥
2.24.m:
This indeed is regarded as the first among all sacrifices, namely the Soma [sacrifice];
with Soma one should worship the deity, the great Lord of the world of Soma.

2.24.s:
na somayāgādadhiko maheśārādhane kratuḥ /
samo vā vidyate tasmāt somenābhyarcayet param //
2.24.d:
न सोमयागादधिको महेशाराधने क्रतुः ।
समो वा विद्यते तस्मात् सोमेनाभ्यर्चयेत् परम् ॥
2.24.m:
There is no sacrifice greater than the Soma sacrifice in worshipping the Great Lord,
nor one equal to it; therefore, one should worship the Supreme [Lord] with Soma.

2.24.s:
pitāmahena viprāṇāmādāvabhihitaḥ śubhaḥ /
dharmo vimuktaye sākṣācchrautaḥ smārto dvidhā punaḥ //
2.24.d:
पितामहेन विप्राणामादावभिहितः शुभः ।
धर्मो विमुक्तये साक्षाच्छ्रौतः स्मार्तो द्विधा पुनः ॥
2.24.m:
In the beginning, auspicious duty was declared by the Grandfather to the Brahmins
for direct liberation, which is two-fold again: scriptural and traditional.

2.24.s:
śrautastretāgnisaṃbandhāt smārtaḥ pūrvaṃ mayoditaḥ /
śreyaskaratamaḥ śrautastasmācchrautaṃ samācaret //
2.24.d:
श्रौतस्त्रेताग्निसंबन्धात् स्मार्तः पूर्वं मयोदितः ।
श्रेयस्करतमः श्रौतस्तस्माच्छ्रौतं समाचरेत् ॥
2.24.m:
The scriptural is connected to the triad of fires; the traditional was previously spoken by me.
The scriptural is the most conducive to welfare; therefore, one should practice the scriptural.

2.24.s:
ubhāvabhihitau dharmau vedādeva viniḥ sṛtau /
śiṣṭācārastṛtīyaḥ syācchratismṛtyoralābhataḥ //
2.24.d:
उभावभिहितौ धर्मौ वेदादेव विनिः सृतौ ।
शिष्टाचारस्तृतीयः स्याच्छ्रतिस्मृत्योरलाभतः ॥
2.24.m:
Both duties described have emerged from the Veda itself;
the conduct of the virtuous is the third, in the absence of scripture and tradition.

2.24.s:
dharmeṇābhigato yaistu vedaḥ saparibṛṃhaṇaḥ /
te śiṣṭā brāhmaṇāḥ proktā nityamātmaguṇānvitāḥ //
2.24.d:
धर्मेणाभिगतो यैस्तु वेदः सपरिबृंहणः ।
ते शिष्टा ब्राह्मणाः प्रोक्ता नित्यमात्मगुणान्विताः ॥
2.24.m:
Those by whom the Veda along with its supplements has been acquired through duty
are declared to be the virtuous Brahmins, constantly endowed with the qualities of the self.

2.24.s:
teṣāmabhimato yaḥ syāccetasā nityameva hi /
sa dharmaḥ kathitaḥ sadbhirnānyeṣāmiti dhāraṇā //
2.24.d:
तेषामभिमतो यः स्याच्चेतसा नित्यमेव हि ।
स धर्मः कथितः सद्भिर्नान्येषामिति धारणा ॥
2.24.m:
Whatever is approved by them in their mind constantly, indeed,
that is declared as duty by the good; not that of others—such is the precept.

2.24.s:
purāṇaṃ dharmaśāstraṃ ca vedānāmupabṛṃhaṇam /
ekasmād brahmavijñānaṃ dharmajñānaṃ tathaikataḥ //
2.24.d:
पुराणं धर्मशास्त्रं च वेदानामुपबृंहणम् ।
एकस्माद् ब्रह्मविज्ञानं धर्मज्ञानं तथैकतः ॥
2.24.m:
The Purāṇa and the Dharmaśāstra are the elaboration of the Vedas:
from the one comes knowledge of Brahman, and from the other knowledge of duty.

2.24.s:
dharmaṃ jijñāsamānānāṃ tatpramāṇataraṃ smṛtam /
dharmaśāstraṃ purāṇaṃ tad brahmajñāne parā pramā //
2.24.d:
धर्मं जिज्ञासमानानां तत्प्रमाणतरं स्मृतम् ।
धर्मशास्त्रं पुराणं तद् ब्रह्मज्ञाने परा प्रमा ॥
2.24.m:
For those desiring to understand duty, that [Dharmaśāstra] is considered the higher authority;
the Dharmaśāstra and that Purāṇa are the supreme authority regarding the knowledge of Brahman.

2.24.s:
nānyato jāyate dharmo brahmavidyā ca vaidikī /
tasmād dharmaṃ purāṇaṃ ca śraddhātavyaṃ dvijātibhiḥ //
iti śrīkūrmapurāṇe ṣaṭsāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāmuparivibhāge caturviśo 'dhyāyaḥ
IN REE NICHT ZULÄSSIGE ZEICHEN:
2.24.d:
नान्यतो जायते धर्मो ब्रह्मविद्या च वैदिकी ।
तस्माद् धर्मं पुराणं च श्रद्धातव्यं द्विजातिभिः ॥
इति श्रीकूर्मपुराणे षट्साहस्त्र्यां संहितायामुपरिविभागे चतुर्विशो ऽध्यायः
इन् रेए निछ्त् Zउल्Äस्सिगे Zएइछेन्:

2.25.s:
vyāsa uvāca
eṣa vo 'bhihitaḥ kṛtsno gṛhasthāśramavāsinaḥ /
dvijāteḥ paramo dharmo vartanāni nibodhata //
2.25.d:
व्यास उवाच
एष वो ऽभिहितः कृत्स्नो गृहस्थाश्रमवासिनः ।
द्विजातेः परमो धर्मो वर्तनानि निबोधत ॥
2.25.m:
Vyāsa said:
This entire supreme duty of the twice-born dwelling in the stage of the householder
has been declared to you; now learn their means of livelihood.

2.25.s:
dvividhastu gṛhī jñeyaḥ sādhakaścāpyasādhakaḥ /
adhyāpanaṃ yājanaṃ ca pūrvasyāhuḥ pratigraham /
kusīdakṛṣivāṇijyaṃ prakurvotāsvayaṅkṛtam //
2.25.d:
द्विविधस्तु गृही ज्ञेयः साधकश्चाप्यसाधकः ।
अध्यापनं याजनं च पूर्वस्याहुः प्रतिग्रहम् ।
कुसीदकृषिवाणिज्यं प्रकुर्वोतास्वयङ्कृतम् ॥

2.25.s:
kṛṣerabhāvād vāṇijyaṃ tadabhāvāt kusīdakam /
āpatkalpo hyaṃ jñeyaḥ pūrvokto mukhya iṣyate //
2.25.d:
कृषेरभावाद् वाणिज्यं तदभावात् कुसीदकम् ।
आपत्कल्पो ह्यं ज्ञेयः पूर्वोक्तो मुख्य इष्यते ॥
2.25.m:
In the absence of agriculture, [he may pursue] commerce; in the absence of that, usury.
For this is to be known as a procedure for times of distress; the previously mentioned is considered primary.

2.25.s:
svayaṃ vā karṣaṇaṃ kuryād vāṇijyaṃ vā kusīdakam /
kaṣṭā pāpīyasī vṛttiḥ kusīdaṃ tad vivarjayet //
2.25.d:
स्वयं वा कर्षणं कुर्याद् वाणिज्यं वा कुसीदकम् ।
कष्टा पापीयसी वृत्तिः कुसीदं तद् विवर्जयेत् ॥
2.25.m:
Or he may personally perform ploughing, or trade, or usury;
usury is a painful, most sinful livelihood; he should abandon that.

2.25.s:
kṣātravṛttiṃ parāṃ prahurna svayaṃ karṣaṇaṃ dvijaiḥ /
tasmāt kṣātreṇa varteta vartanenāpadi dvijaḥ //
2.25.d:
क्षात्रवृत्तिं परां प्रहुर्न स्वयं कर्षणं द्विजैः ।
तस्मात् क्षात्रेण वर्तेत वर्तनेनापदि द्विजः ॥
2.25.m:
They declare the livelihood of a Kṣatriya to be superior, not ploughing done by twice-born themselves;
therefore, in times of distress, a twice-born may maintain himself by the livelihood of a Kṣatriya.

2.25.s:
tena cāvāpyajīvaṃstu vaiśyavṛttiṃ kṛṣiṃ vrajet /
na kathañcana kurvota brāhmaṇaḥ karma karṣaṇam //
2.25.d:
तेन चावाप्यजीवंस्तु वैश्यवृत्तिं कृषिं व्रजेत् ।
न कथञ्चन कुर्वोत ब्राह्मणः कर्म कर्षणम् ॥
2.25.m:
And if unable to obtain a livelihood through that, he may go to agriculture, the livelihood of a Vaiśya;
under no circumstances should a Brahmin perform the work of ploughing [himself].

2.25.s:
labdhalābhaḥ pitṝn devān brāhmaṇāṃścāpi pūjayet /
te tṛptāstasya taṃ doṣaṃ śamayanti na saṃśayaḥ //
2.25.d:
लब्धलाभः पितॄन् देवान् ब्राह्मणांश्चापि पूजयेत् ।
ते तृप्तास्तस्य तं दोषं शमयन्ति न संशयः ॥
2.25.m:
Having obtained profit, he should also worship the ancestors, the gods, and the Brahmins;
they, being satisfied, dispel that fault of his, without doubt.

2.25.s:
devebhyaśca pitṛbhyaśca dadyād bhāgaṃ tu viṃśakam /
triṃśadbhāgaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ kṛṣiṃ kurvan na duṣyati //
2.25.d:
देवेभ्यश्च पितृभ्यश्च दद्याद् भागं तु विंशकम् ।
त्रिंशद्भागं ब्राह्मणानां कृषिं कुर्वन् न दुष्यति ॥
2.25.m:
He should give a twentieth portion to the gods and the ancestors,
and a thirtieth portion to Brahmins; practicing agriculture, he does not incur fault.

2.25.s:
vaṇik pradadyād dviguṇaṃ kusīdī triguṇaṃ punaḥ /
kṛṣīvalo na doṣeṇa yujyate nātra saṃśayaḥ //
2.25.d:
वणिक् प्रदद्याद् द्विगुणं कुसीदी त्रिगुणं पुनः ।
कृषीवलो न दोषेण युज्यते नात्र संशयः ॥
2.25.m:
A merchant should give twice that, and a usurer thrice that;
the cultivator is not associated with fault; there is no doubt in this.

2.25.s:
śiloñchaṃ vāpyādadīta gṛhasthaḥ sādhakaḥ punaḥ /
vidyāśilpādayastvanye bahavo vṛttihetavaḥ //
2.25.d:
शिलोञ्छं वाप्याददीत गृहस्थः साधकः पुनः ।
विद्याशिल्पादयस्त्वन्ये बहवो वृत्तिहेतवः ॥
2.25.m:
Or the practicing householder may adopt gleaning and collecting ears of grain;
there are, however, many other means of livelihood such as learning and crafts.

2.25.s:
asādhakastu yaḥ prokto gṛhasthāśramasaṃsthitaḥ /
śiloñche tasya kathite dve vṛttī paramarṣibhiḥ //
2.25.d:
असाधकस्तु यः प्रोक्तो गृहस्थाश्रमसंस्थितः ।
शिलोञ्छे तस्य कथिते द्वे वृत्ती परमर्षिभिः ॥
2.25.m:
As for the one who is declared a non-practitioner living in the stage of the householder,
two livelihoods have been stated for him by the supreme sages: gleaning and collecting ears of grain.

2.25.s:
amṛtenāthavā jīvenmṛtenāpyathavā yadi /
ayācitaṃ syādamṛtaṃ mṛtaṃ bhekṣaṃ tu yācitam //
2.25.d:
अमृतेनाथवा जीवेन्मृतेनाप्यथवा यदि ।
अयाचितं स्यादमृतं मृतं भेक्षं तु याचितम् ॥
2.25.m:
Or he may live by the 'nectar', or else if he chooses, by the 'dead';
what is unasked would be the 'nectar', while the 'dead' is food obtained by begging.

2.25.s:
kuśūladhānyako vā syāt kumbhīdhānyaka eva vā /
tryahaihiko vāpi bhavedaśvastanika eva ca //
2.25.d:
कुशूलधान्यको वा स्यात् कुम्भीधान्यक एव वा ।
त्र्यहैहिको वापि भवेदश्वस्तनिक एव च ॥
2.25.m:
He may have grain enough for a granary, or he may have grain enough for a jar,
or he may have grain for three days, or he may have nothing for tomorrow.

2.25.s:
caturṇāmapi caiteṣāṃ dvijānāṃ gṛhamedhinām /
śreyān paraḥ paro jñeyo dharmato lokajittamaḥ //
2.25.d:
चतुर्णामपि चैतेषां द्विजानां गृहमेधिनाम् ।
श्रेयान् परः परो ज्ञेयो धर्मतो लोकजित्तमः ॥
2.25.m:
Even among these four householder twice-born,
each subsequent one is to be known as superior in duty and the greatest conqueror of worlds.

2.25.s:
ṣaṭkarmaiko bhavatyeṣāṃ tribhiranyaḥ pravartate /
dvābhyāmekaścaturthastu brahmasatreṇa jīvati //
2.25.d:
षट्कर्मैको भवत्येषां त्रिभिरन्यः प्रवर्तते ।
द्वाभ्यामेकश्चतुर्थस्तु ब्रह्मसत्रेण जीवति ॥
2.25.m:
One of these engages in the six duties; another proceeds with three;
one with two, while the fourth lives by the sacrifice to Brahman.

2.25.s:
vartayaṃstu śiloñchābhyāmagnihotraparāyaṇaḥ /
iṣṭīḥ pārvāyaṇāntīyāḥ kevalā nirvapet sadā //
2.25.d:
वर्तयंस्तु शिलोञ्छाभ्यामग्निहोत्रपरायणः ।
इष्टीः पार्वायणान्तीयाः केवला निर्वपेत् सदा ॥
2.25.m:
Maintaining himself by gleaning and collecting ears of grain, devoted to the Agnihotra,
he should always offer only the sacrifices ending at the full and new moon.

2.25.s:
na lokavṛtiṃ varteta vṛttihetoḥ kathañcana /
ajihmāmaśaṭhāṃ śuddhāṃ jīved brāhmaṇajīvikām //
2.25.d:
न लोकवृतिं वर्तेत वृत्तिहेतोः कथञ्चन ।
अजिह्मामशठां शुद्धां जीवेद् ब्राह्मणजीविकाम् ॥
2.25.m:
He should under no circumstances live by worldly conduct for the sake of livelihood;
he should live by a straightforward, honest, pure Brahmin livelihood.

2.25.s:
yācitvā vāpi sadbhyo 'nnaṃ pitṝndevāṃstu toṣayet /
yācayed vā śuciṃ dāntaṃ na tṛpyeta svayaṃ tataḥ //
2.25.d:
याचित्वा वापि सद्भ्यो ऽन्नं पितॄन्देवांस्तु तोषयेत् ।
याचयेद् वा शुचिं दान्तं न तृप्येत स्वयं ततः ॥
2.25.m:
Or, having begged food from the virtuous, he should satisfy the ancestors and the gods;
or he may beg from one who is pure and restrained, but should not satisfy himself from that.

2.25.s:
yastu dravyārjanaṃ kṛtvā gṛhasthastoṣayenna tu /
devān pitṛṃśca vidhinā śunāṃ yoniṃ vrajatyasau //
2.25.d:
यस्तु द्रव्यार्जनं कृत्वा गृहस्थस्तोषयेन्न तु ।
देवान् पितृंश्च विधिना शुनां योनिं व्रजत्यसौ ॥
2.25.m:
A householder who, having acquired wealth, does not satisfy
the gods and ancestors according to the rule, goes to the womb of dogs.

2.25.s:
dharmaścārthaśca kāmaśca śreyo mokṣaścatuṣṭayam /
dharmāviruddhaḥ kāmaḥ syād brāhmaṇānāṃ tu netaraḥ //
2.25.d:
धर्मश्चार्थश्च कामश्च श्रेयो मोक्षश्चतुष्टयम् ।
धर्माविरुद्धः कामः स्याद् ब्राह्मणानां तु नेतरः ॥
2.25.m:
Duty, wealth, pleasure, and liberation are the four-fold welfare;
for Brahmins, pleasure must not be opposed to duty, but no other.

2.25.s:
yor'tho dharmāya nātmārthaḥ sor'tho 'narthastathetaraḥ /
tasmādarthaṃ samāsādya dadyād vai juhuyād yajet //
iti śrīkūrmapurāṇe ṣaṭsāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāmuparivibhāge pañcaviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
IN REE NICHT ZULÄSSIGE ZEICHEN:
2.25.d:
योर्ऽथो धर्माय नात्मार्थः सोर्ऽथो ऽनर्थस्तथेतरः ।
तस्मादर्थं समासाद्य दद्याद् वै जुहुयाद् यजेत् ॥
इति श्रीकूर्मपुराणे षट्साहस्त्र्यां संहितायामुपरिविभागे पञ्चविंशो ऽध्यायः
इन् रेए निछ्त् Zउल्Äस्सिगे Zएइछेन्:
2.25.m:
That wealth which is not for duty, but for oneself, is a calamity; and likewise the other.
Therefore, having obtained wealth, one should give, offer into the fire, and sacrifice.

Thus ends the twenty-fifth chapter in the latter section of the compilation of six thousand verses in the glorious Kūrma Purāṇa.

2.26.s:
vyāsa uvāca
athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi dānadharmamanuttamam /
brahmaṇābhihitaṃ pūrvamṛṣīṇāṃ brahmavādinām //
2.26.d:
व्यास उवाच
अथातः संप्रवक्ष्यामि दानधर्ममनुत्तमम् ।
ब्रह्मणाभिहितं पूर्वमृषीणां ब्रह्मवादिनाम् ॥
2.26.m:
Vyāsa said:
Now therefore I shall proclaim the unsurpassed duty of giving,
which was declared of old by Brahmā to the sages who proclaim Brahman.

2.26.s:
arthānāmudite pātre śraddhayā pratipādanam /
dānamityabhinirdiṣṭaṃ bhuktimuktiphalapradam //
2.26.d:
अर्थानामुदिते पात्रे श्रद्धया प्रतिपादनम् ।
दानमित्यभिनिर्दिष्टं भुक्तिमुक्तिफलप्रदम् ॥
2.26.m:
Bestowing wealth upon a worthy recipient with faith
is defined as gift, which grants the fruits of enjoyment and liberation.

2.26.s:
yad dadāti viśiṣṭebhyaḥ śraddhayā parayā yutaḥ /
tad vai vittamahaṃ manye śeṣaṃ kasyāpi rakṣati //
2.26.d:
यद् ददाति विशिष्टेभ्यः श्रद्धया परया युतः ।
तद् वै वित्तमहं मन्ये शेषं कस्यापि रक्षति ॥
2.26.m:
What one gives to distinguished men endowed with supreme faith,
that indeed I consider real wealth; the remainder one preserves for someone else.

2.26.s:
nityaṃ naimittikaṃ kāmyaṃ trividhaṃ dānamucyate /
caturthaṃ vimalaṃ proktaṃ sarvadānottamottamam //
2.26.d:
नित्यं नैमित्तिकं काम्यं त्रिविधं दानमुच्यते ।
चतुर्थं विमलं प्रोक्तं सर्वदानोत्तमोत्तमम् ॥
2.26.m:
Gift is said to be three-fold: regular, occasional, and optional;
a fourth is declared as the pure, the highest of the high among all gifts.

2.26.s:
ahanyahani yat kiñcid dīyate 'nupakāriṇe /
anuddiśya phalaṃ tasmād brāhmaṇāya tu nityakam //
2.26.d:
अहन्यहनि यत् किञ्चिद् दीयते ऽनुपकारिणे ।
अनुद्दिश्य फलं तस्माद् ब्राह्मणाय तु नित्यकम् ॥
2.26.m:
Whatever is given day by day to one who has done no service,
without anticipating any fruit from it, to a Brahmin, is the regular [gift].

2.26.s:
yat tu pāpopaśāntyarthaṃ dīyate viduṣāṃ kare /
naimittikaṃ taduddiṣṭaṃ dānaṃ sadbhiranuṣṭhitam //
2.26.d:
यत् तु पापोपशान्त्यर्थं दीयते विदुषां करे ।
नैमित्तिकं तदुद्दिष्टं दानं सद्भिरनुष्ठितम् ॥
2.26.m:
That which is given into the hand of wise men for the pacification of sin,
performed by the virtuous, is designated as the occasional gift.

2.26.s:
apatyavijayaiśvaryasvargārthaṃ yat pradīyate /
dānaṃ tat kāmyamākhyātamṛṣibhirdharmacintakaiḥ //
2.26.d:
अपत्यविजयैश्वर्यस्वर्गार्थं यत् प्रदीयते ।
दानं तत् काम्यमाख्यातमृषिभिर्धर्मचिन्तकैः ॥
2.26.m: That gift which is bestowed for the sake of offspring, victory, sovereignty, or heaven / is declared by the sages, contemplators of duty, to be optional.

2.26.s:
yadīśvaraprīṇanārthaṃ brahmavitsu pradīyate /
cetasā dharmayuktena dānaṃ tad vimalaṃ śivam //
2.26.d:
यदीश्वरप्रीणनार्थं ब्रह्मवित्सु प्रदीयते ।
चेतसा धर्मयुक्तेन दानं तद् विमलं शिवम् ॥
2.26.m: That which is bestowed upon knowers of Brahman to propitiate the Lord, / with a mind intent on righteousness, is pure and auspicious.

2.26.s:
dānadharmaṃ niṣeveta pātramāsādya śaktitaḥ /
utpatsyate hi tatpātraṃ yat tārayati sarvataḥ //
2.26.d:
दानधर्मं निषेवेत पात्रमासाद्य शक्तितः ।
उत्पत्स्यते हि तत्पात्रं यत् तारयति सर्वतः ॥
2.26.m: One should practice the duty of giving according to one's capacity, having found a worthy recipient; / for that worthy recipient will arise who delivers [the giver] in every way.

2.26.s:
kuṭumbabhaktavasanād deyaṃ yadatiricyate /
anyathā dīyate yaddhi na tad dānaṃ phalapradam //
2.26.d:
कुटुम्बभक्तवसनाद् देयं यदतिरिच्यते ।
अन्यथा दीयते यद्धि न तद् दानं फलप्रदम् ॥
2.26.m: Whatever remains over and above the food and clothing of one's family should be given; / for what is given otherwise is not a gift that yields fruit.

2.26.s:
śrotriyāya kulīnāya vinītāya tapasvine /
vṛttasthāya daridrāya pradeyaṃ bhaktipūrvakam //
2.26.d:
श्रोत्रियाय कुलीनाय विनीताय तपस्विने ।
वृत्तस्थाय दरिद्राय प्रदेयं भक्तिपूर्वकम् ॥
2.26.m: To a Vedic scholar, well-born, disciplined, ascetic, / established in good conduct, and poor, one should give with devotion.

2.26.s:
yastu dadyānmahīṃ bhaktyā brāhmaṇāyāhitāgnaye /
sa yāti paramaṃ sthānaṃ yatra gatvā na śocati //
2.26.d:
यस्तु दद्यान्महीं भक्त्या ब्राह्मणायाहिताग्नये ।
स याति परमं स्थानं यत्र गत्वा न शोचति ॥
2.26.m: He who devoutly gives land to a Brāhmaṇa who maintains the sacred fires / goes to the supreme abode, reaching which he grieves no more.

2.26.s:
ikṣubhiḥ saṃtatāṃ bhumiṃ yavagodhūmaśalinīm /
dadāti vedaviduṣe yaḥ sa bhūyo na jāyate //
2.26.d:
इक्षुभिः संततां भुमिं यवगोधूमशलिनीम् ।
ददाति वेदविदुषे यः स भूयो न जायते ॥
2.26.m: He who gives to a knower of the Vedas land covered with sugarcane / and rich in barley and wheat is not born again.

2.26.s:
gocarmamātrāmapi vā yo bhūmiṃ saṃprayacchati /
brāhmaṇāya daridrāya sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate //
2.26.d:
गोचर्ममात्रामपि वा यो भूमिं संप्रयच्छति ।
ब्राह्मणाय दरिद्राय सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥
2.26.m: He who presents even a cow-hide measure of land / to a poor Brāhmaṇa is freed from all sins.

2.26.s:
bhūmidānāt paraṃ dānaṃ vidyate neha kiñcana /
annadānaṃ tena tulyaṃ vidyādānaṃ tato 'dhikam //
2.26.d:
भूमिदानात् परं दानं विद्यते नेह किञ्चन ।
अन्नदानं तेन तुल्यं विद्यादानं ततो ऽधिकम् ॥
2.26.m: No gift in this world is superior to a gift of land; / the gift of food is equal to it, and the gift of knowledge is greater still.

2.26.s:
yo brāhmaṇāya śāntāya śucaye dharmaśāline /
dadāti vidyāṃ vidhinā brahmaloke mahīyate //
2.26.d:
यो ब्राह्मणाय शान्ताय शुचये धर्मशालिने ।
ददाति विद्यां विधिना ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ॥
2.26.m: He who gives knowledge according to rule to a peaceful, / pure, and righteous Brāhmaṇa is exalted in the realm of Brahmā.

2.26.s:
dadyādaharahastvannaṃ śraddhayā brahmacāriṇe /
sarvapāpavinirmukto brahmaṇaḥ sthānamāpnuyāt //
2.26.d:
दद्यादहरहस्त्वन्नं श्रद्धया ब्रह्मचारिणे ।
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तो ब्रह्मणः स्थानमाप्नुयात् ॥
2.26.m: Day by day one should give food with faith to a student of the Vedas; / freed from all sins, he attains the abode of Brahmā.

2.26.s:
gṛhasthāyānnadānena phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ /
āmamevāsya dātavyaṃ dattvāpnoti parāṃ gatim //
2.26.d:
गृहस्थायान्नदानेन फलं प्राप्नोति मानवः ।
आममेवास्य दातव्यं दत्त्वाप्नोति परां गतिम् ॥
2.26.m: By giving food to a householder, a man attains a reward; / raw [food] alone should be given to him, and having given it, he attains the supreme state.

2.26.s:
vaiśākhyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ tu brāhmaṇān sapta pañca vā /
upoṣya vidhinā śāntaḥ śuciḥ prayatamānasaḥ //
2.26.d:
वैशाख्यां पौर्णमास्यां तु ब्राह्मणान् सप्त पञ्च वा ।
उपोष्य विधिना शान्तः शुचिः प्रयतमानसः ॥
2.26.m: On the full moon of Vaiśākha, having fasted according to rule, peaceful, / pure, and restrained in mind, [approaching] five or seven Brāhmaṇas,

2.26.s:
pūjayitvā tilaiḥ kṛṣṇairmadhunā na viśeṣataḥ /
gandhādibhiḥ samabhyarcya vācayed vā svyaṃ vadet //
2.26.d:
पूजयित्वा तिलैः कृष्णैर्मधुना न विशेषतः ।
गन्धादिभिः समभ्यर्च्य वाचयेद् वा स्व्यं वदेत् ॥
2.26.m: and having honoured them especially with black sesame seeds and honey, / worshipping them with perfumes and other offerings, he should recite or say himself:

2.26.s:
prīyatāṃ dharmarājeti yad vā manasi vartate /
yāvajjīvakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ tatkṣaṇādeva naśyati //
2.26.d:
प्रीयतां धर्मराजेति यद् वा मनसि वर्तते ।
यावज्जीवकृतं पापं तत्क्षणादेव नश्यति ॥
2.26.m: “May the King of Justice be pleased,” or whatever is in his heart; / the sin committed throughout his life is destroyed that very moment.

2.26.s:
kṛṣṇājine tilān kṛttvā hiraṇyaṃ madhusarpiṣī /
dadāti yastu viprāya sarvaṃ tarati duṣkṛtam //
2.26.d:
कृष्णाजिने तिलान् कृत्त्वा हिरण्यं मधुसर्पिषी ।
ददाति यस्तु विप्राय सर्वं तरति दुष्कृतम् ॥
2.26.m: He who, having placed sesame seeds, gold, honey, and clarified butter on a black antelope skin, / gives it to a Brāhmaṇa, overcomes all wrongdoing.

2.26.s:
kṛtānnamudakumbhaṃ ca vaiśākhyāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ /
nirdiśya dharmarājāya viprebhyo mucyate bhayāt //
2.26.d:
कृतान्नमुदकुम्भं च वैशाख्यां च विशेषतः ।
निर्दिश्य धर्मराजाय विप्रेभ्यो मुच्यते भयात् ॥
2.26.m: Especially on the full moon of Vaiśākha, having dedicated cooked food / and a water-jar to the King of Justice, [and giving them] to Brāhmaṇas, he is freed from fear.

2.26.s:
suvarṇatilayuktaistu brāhmaṇān sapta pañca vā /
tarpayedudapātraistu brahmahatyāṃ vyapohati //
2.26.d:
सुवर्णतिलयुक्तैस्तु ब्राह्मणान् सप्त पञ्च वा ।
तर्पयेदुदपात्रैस्तु ब्रह्महत्यां व्यपोहति ॥
2.26.m: One who gratifies five or seven Brāhmaṇas / with water-vessels together with gold and sesame seeds dispels the killing of a Brāhmaṇa.

2.26.s:
māghamāse tu viprastu dvādaśyāṃ samupoṣitaḥ /
śuklāmvaradharaḥ kṛṣṇaistilairhutvā hutāśanam //
2.26.d:
माघमासे तु विप्रस्तु द्वादश्यां समुपोषितः ।
शुक्लाम्वरधरः कृष्णैस्तिलैर्हुत्वा हुताशनम् ॥
2.26.m: In the month of Māgha, having fasted on the twelfth day, / wearing white garments, offering black sesame seeds into the fire,

2.26.s:
pradadyād brāhmaṇebhyastu tilāneva samāhitaḥ /
janmaprabhṛti yatpāpaṃ sarvaṃ tarati vai dvijaḥ //
2.26.d:
प्रदद्याद् ब्राह्मणेभ्यस्तु तिलानेव समाहितः ।
जन्मप्रभृति यत्पापं सर्वं तरति वै द्विजः ॥
2.26.m: a twice-born should attentively give only sesame seeds to Brāhmaṇas; / he indeed overcomes all sin committed since birth.

2.26.s:
amāvasyāmanuprāpya brāhmaṇāya tapasvine /
yatkicid devadeveśaṃ dadyāccoddiśya śaṅkaram //
2.26.d:
अमावस्यामनुप्राप्य ब्राह्मणाय तपस्विने ।
यत्किचिद् देवदेवेशं दद्याच्चोद्दिश्य शङ्करम् ॥
2.26.m: When the new moon arrives, whatever one might give to an ascetic Brāhmaṇa, / dedicating it to Śaṅkara, the lord of the god of gods, [with the words:]

2.26.s:
prīyatāmīśvaraḥ somo mahādevaḥ sanātanaḥ /
saptajanmakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ tatkṣaṇādeva naśyati //
2.26.d:
प्रीयतामीश्वरः सोमो महादेवः सनातनः ।
सप्तजन्मकृतं पापं तत्क्षणादेव नश्यति ॥
2.26.m: “May the Lord, Soma, the eternal Mahādeva, be pleased,” / the sin committed across seven births is destroyed that very moment.

2.26.s:
yastu kṛṣṇacaturdaśyāṃ snātvā devaṃ pinākinam /
ārādhayed dvijamukhe na tasyāsti punarbhavaḥ //
2.26.d:
यस्तु कृष्णचतुर्दश्यां स्नात्वा देवं पिनाकिनम् ।
आराधयेद् द्विजमुखे न तस्यास्ति पुनर्भवः ॥
2.26.m: He who, having bathed on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, / worships the bow-wielding god through the mouth of a twice-born, has no rebirth.

2.26.s:
kṛṣṇāṣṭamyāṃ viśeṣeṇa dhārmikāya dvijātaye /
snātvābhyarcya yathānyāyaṃ pādaprakṣālanādibhiḥ //
2.26.d:
कृष्णाष्टम्यां विशेषेण धार्मिकाय द्विजातये ।
स्नात्वाभ्यर्च्य यथान्यायं पादप्रक्षालनादिभिः ॥
2.26.m: Especially on the eighth day of the dark fortnight, to a righteous twice-born, / having bathed and worshipped according to rule with washing of the feet and other rites,

2.26.s:
prīyatāṃ me mahādevo dadyād dravyaṃ svakīyakam /
sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ prāpnoti paramāṃ gatim //
2.26.d:
प्रीयतां मे महादेवो दद्याद् द्रव्यं स्वकीयकम् ।
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तः प्राप्नोति परमां गतिम् ॥
2.26.m: [saying,] “May Mahādeva be pleased with me,” he should give his own wealth; / freed from all sins, he attains the supreme state.

2.26.s:
dvijaiḥ kṛṣṇacaturdaśyāṃ kṛṣṇāṣṭamyāṃ viśeṣataḥ /
amāvāsyāyāṃ bhaktaistu pūjanīyastrilocanaḥ //
2.26.d:
द्विजैः कृष्णचतुर्दश्यां कृष्णाष्टम्यां विशेषतः ।
अमावास्यायां भक्तैस्तु पूजनीयस्त्रिलोचनः ॥
2.26.m: The three-eyed god should be worshipped by devotees among the twice-born / especially on the fourteenth of the dark fortnight, on the eighth of the dark fortnight, and on the new moon.

2.26.s:
ekādaśyāṃ nirāhāro dvādaśyāṃ puruṣottamam /
arcayed bāhmaṇamukhe sa gacchet paramaṃ padam //
2.26.d:
एकादश्यां निराहारो द्वादश्यां पुरुषोत्तमम् ।
अर्चयेद् बाह्मणमुखे स गच्छेत् परमं पदम् ॥
2.26.m: Fasting on the eleventh day, he who worships the Supreme Spirit on the twelfth day / through the mouth of a Brāhmaṇa goes to the supreme abode.

2.26.s:
eṣā tithirvaiṣṇavīṃ syād dvādaśī śuklapakṣake /
tasyāmārādhayed devaṃ prayatnena janārdanam //
2.26.d:
एषा तिथिर्वैष्णवीं स्याद् द्वादशी शुक्लपक्षके ।
तस्यामाराधयेद् देवं प्रयत्नेन जनार्दनम् ॥
2.26.m: This twelfth day in the bright fortnight is sacred to Viṣṇu; / on it one should worship the divine Janārdana with effort.

2.26.s:
yatkiñcid devamīśānamuddiśya brāhmaṇe śucau /
dīyate viṣṇave vāpi tadanantaphalapradam //
2.26.d:
यत्किञ्चिद् देवमीशानमुद्दिश्य ब्राह्मणे शुचौ ।
दीयते विष्णवे वापि तदनन्तफलप्रदम् ॥
2.26.m: Whatever is given to a pure Brāhmaṇa, / dedicated to the divine Īśāna or to Viṣṇu, grants infinite fruit.

2.26.s:
yo hi yāṃ devatāmicchet samārādhayituṃ naraḥ /
brāhmaṇān pūjayed yatnāt satasyāṃ toṣayet tataḥ //
2.26.d:
यो हि यां देवतामिच्छेत् समाराधयितुं नरः ।
ब्राह्मणान् पूजयेद् यत्नात् सतस्यां तोषयेत् ततः ॥
2.26.m: Whatever deity a man wishes to worship, / he should diligently worship Brāhmaṇas; thereby he pleases that [deity].

2.26.s:
dvijānāṃ vapurāsthāya nityaṃ tiṣṭhanti devatāḥ /
pūjyante brāhmaṇālābhe pratimādiṣvapi kvacit //
2.26.d:
द्विजानां वपुरास्थाय नित्यं तिष्ठन्ति देवताः ।
पूज्यन्ते ब्राह्मणालाभे प्रतिमादिष्वपि क्वचित् ॥
2.26.m: Taking the bodies of the twice-born, deities reside constantly; / in the absence of a Brāhmaṇa, they are sometimes worshipped in images and the like.

2.26.s:
tasmāt sarvaprayatnena tat tat phalamabhīpsatā /
dvijeṣu devatā nityaṃ pūjanīyā viśeṣataḥ //
2.26.d:
तस्मात् सर्वप्रयत्नेन तत् तत् फलमभीप्सता ।
द्विजेषु देवता नित्यं पूजनीया विशेषतः ॥
2.26.m: Therefore, by one desiring this or that fruit with every effort, / the deities should constantly be worshipped especially in the twice-born.

2.26.s:
vibhūtikāmaḥ satataṃ pūjayed vai purandaram /
brahmavarcasakāmastu brahmāṇaṃ brahmakāmukaḥ //
2.26.d:
विभूतिकामः सततं पूजयेद् वै पुरन्दरम् ।
ब्रह्मवर्चसकामस्तु ब्रह्माणं ब्रह्मकामुकः ॥
2.26.m: One who desires prosperity should constantly worship Purandara; / one who desires Vedic splendor should worship Brahmā; one who desires Brahman [should worship Brahmā];

2.26.s:
ārogyakāmo 'tha raviṃ dhanakāmo hutāśanam /
karmaṇāṃ siddhikāmastu pūjayed vai vināyakam //
2.26.d:
आरोग्यकामो ऽथ रविं धनकामो हुताशनम् ।
कर्मणां सिद्धिकामस्तु पूजयेद् वै विनायकम् ॥
2.26.m: one who desires health, the Sun; one who desires wealth, Fire; / one who desires the success of undertakings should worship Vināyaka;

2.26.s:
bhogakāmastu śaśinaṃ balakāmaḥ samīraṇam /
mumukṣuḥ sarvasaṃsārāt prayatnenārcayeddharim //
2.26.d:
भोगकामस्तु शशिनं बलकामः समीरणम् ।
मुमुक्षुः सर्वसंसारात् प्रयत्नेनार्चयेद्धरिम् ॥
2.26.m: one who desires enjoyment, the Moon; one who desires strength, the Wind; / a seeker of liberation from all worldly existence should worship Hari with effort.

2.26.s:
yastu yogaṃ tathā mokṣamanvicchejjñānamaiśvaram /
sor'cayed vai virūpākṣaṃ prayatneneśvareśvaram //
2.26.d:
यस्तु योगं तथा मोक्षमन्विच्छेज्ज्ञानमैश्वरम् ।
सोर्ऽचयेद् वै विरूपाक्षं प्रयत्नेनेश्वरेश्वरम् ॥
2.26.m: He who seeks yoga, liberation, and divine knowledge / should diligently worship the odd-eyed god, the lord of lords.

2.26.s:
ye vāñchanti mahāyogān jñānāni ca maheśvaram /
te pūjayanti bhūteśaṃ keśavaṃ cāpi bhoginaḥ //
2.26.d:
ये वाञ्छन्ति महायोगान् ज्ञानानि च महेश्वरम् ।
ते पूजयन्ति भूतेशं केशवं चापि भोगिनः ॥
2.26.m: Those who desire great yogas and knowledge worship Maheśvara, / the lord of beings, while enjoyers worship Keśava.

2.26.s:
vāridastṛptimāpnoti sukhamakṣayyamannadaḥ /
tilapradaḥ prajāmiṣṭāṃ dīpadaścakṣuruttamam //
2.26.d:
वारिदस्तृप्तिमाप्नोति सुखमक्षय्यमन्नदः ।
तिलप्रदः प्रजामिष्टां दीपदश्चक्षुरुत्तमम् ॥
2.26.m: The giver of water attains satisfaction; the giver of food, imperishable happiness; / the giver of sesame seeds, desirable offspring; the giver of a lamp, excellent sight.

2.26.s:
bhūmidaḥ sarvamāpnoti dīrghamāyurhiraṇyadaḥ /
gṛhado 'gryāṇi veśmāni rūpyado rūpamuttamam //
2.26.d:
भूमिदः सर्वमाप्नोति दीर्घमायुर्हिरण्यदः ।
गृहदो ऽग्र्याणि वेश्मानि रूप्यदो रूपमुत्तमम् ॥
2.26.m: The giver of land attains everything; the giver of gold, long life; / the giver of a house, superior dwellings; the giver of silver, excellent beauty.

2.26.s:
vāsodaścandrasālokyamaśvisālokyamaśvadaḥ /
anaḍudaḥ śriyaṃ puṣṭāṃ godo vradhnasya viṣṭapam //
2.26.d:
वासोदश्चन्द्रसालोक्यमश्विसालोक्यमश्वदः ।
अनडुदः श्रियं पुष्टां गोदो व्रध्नस्य विष्टपम् ॥
2.26.m: The giver of clothing [attains] residence in the realm of the Moon; the giver of a horse, residence in the realm of the Aśvins; / the giver of an ox, abundant prosperity; the giver of a cow, the realm of the Sun.

2.26.s:
yānaśayyāprado bhāryāmaiśvaryamabhayapradaḥ /
dhānyadaḥ śāśvataṃ saukhyaṃ brahmado brahmasātmyatām //
2.26.d:
यानशय्याप्रदो भार्यामैश्वर्यमभयप्रदः ।
धान्यदः शाश्वतं सौख्यं ब्रह्मदो ब्रह्मसात्म्यताम् ॥
2.26.m: The giver of a vehicle and a bed [attains] a wife; the giver of security, sovereignty; / the giver of grain, eternal happiness; the giver of the Veda, oneness with Brahman.

2.26.s:
dhānyānyapi yathāśakti vipreṣu pratipādayet /
vedavitsu viśiṣṭeṣu pretya svargaṃ samaśnute //
2.26.d:
धान्यान्यपि यथाशक्ति विप्रेषु प्रतिपादयेत् ।
वेदवित्सु विशिष्टेषु प्रेत्य स्वर्गं समश्नुते ॥
2.26.m: One should also bestow grains according to one's ability on Brāhmaṇas; / [giving them] to distinguished knowers of the Veda, one enjoys heaven after death.

2.26.s:
gavāṃ ghāsapradānena sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate /
indhanānāṃ pradānena dīptāgnirjāyate naraḥ //
2.26.d:
गवां घासप्रदानेन सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ।
इन्धनानां प्रदानेन दीप्ताग्निर्जायते नरः ॥
2.26.m: By giving grass to cows, one is freed from all sins; / by giving firewood, a man becomes endowed with a blazing digestive fire.

2.26.s:
phalamūlāni śākāni bhojyāni vividhāni ca /
pradadyād brāhmaṇebhyastu mudā yuktaḥ sadā bhavet //
2.26.d:
फलमूलानि शाकानि भोज्यानि विविधानि च ।
प्रदद्याद् ब्राह्मणेभ्यस्तु मुदा युक्तः सदा भवेत् ॥
2.26.m: Fruits, roots, vegetables, and various types of food / one should give to Brāhmaṇas; he will always remain filled with joy.

2.26.s:
auṣadhaṃ snehamāhāraṃ rogiṇe rogaśāntaye /
dadāno rogarahitaḥ sukhī dīrghāyureva ca //
2.26.d:
औषधं स्नेहमाहारं रोगिणे रोगशान्तये ।
ददानो रोगरहितः सुखी दीर्घायुरेव च ॥
2.26.m: One who gives medicine, oil, and food to a sick person to alleviate illness / becomes free from illness, happy, and long-lived.

2.26.s:
asipatravanaṃ mārgaṃ kṣuradhārāsamanvitam /
tīvritāpaṃ ca tarati chatropānatprado naraḥ //
2.26.d:
असिपत्रवनं मार्गं क्षुरधारासमन्वितम् ।
तीव्रितापं च तरति छत्रोपानत्प्रदो नरः ॥
2.26.m: A man who gives an umbrella and sandals crosses the path / of the Forest of Sword-like Leaves, sharp with razor edges and intensely scorching.

2.26.s:
yad yadiṣṭatamaṃ loke yaccāpi dayitaṃ gṛhe /
tattad guṇavate deyaṃ tadevākṣyamicchatā //
2.26.d:
यद् यदिष्टतमं लोके यच्चापि दयितं गृहे ।
तत्तद् गुणवते देयं तदेवाक्ष्यमिच्छता ॥
2.26.m: Whatever is most cherished in the world, and whatever is beloved in the home, / that should be given to a virtuous person by one desiring it to be imperishable.

2.26.s:
apane viṣuve caiva grahaṇe candrasūryayoḥ /
saṃkrāntyādiṣu kāleṣu dattaṃ bhavati cākṣayam //
2.26.d:
अपने विषुवे चैव ग्रहणे चन्द्रसूर्ययोः ।
संक्रान्त्यादिषु कालेषु दत्तं भवति चाक्षयम् ॥
2.26.m: At the solstice and the equinox, during an eclipse of the moon or the sun, / and at times such as the transition of the sun, what is given becomes imperishable.

2.26.s:
prayāgādiṣu tīrtheṣu puṇyeṣvāyataneṣu ca /
dattvā cākṣayamāpnoti nadīṣu ca vaneṣu ca //
2.26.d:
प्रयागादिषु तीर्थेषु पुण्येष्वायतनेषु च ।
दत्त्वा चाक्षयमाप्नोति नदीषु च वनेषु च ॥
2.26.m:
And by giving at holy sites such as Prayāga, at sacred temples,
at rivers, and in forests, one attains imperishable [fruit].

2.26.s:
dānadharmāt paro dharmo bhūtānāṃ neha vidyate /
tasmād viprāya dātavyaṃ śrotriyāya dvijātibhiḥ //
2.26.d:
दानधर्मात् परो धर्मो भूतानां नेह विद्यते ।
तस्माद् विप्राय दातव्यं श्रोत्रियाय द्विजातिभिः ॥
2.26.m:
There is no higher duty for living beings here than the duty of giving;
therefore, twice-born people must give to a learned brāhmaṇa.

2.26.s:
svagāyurbhūtikāmena tathā pāpopaśāntaye /
mumukṣuṇā ca dātavyaṃ brāhmaṇebhyastathānvaham //
2.26.d:
स्वगायुर्भूतिकामेन तथा पापोपशान्तये ।
मुमुक्षुणा च दातव्यं ब्राह्मणेभ्यस्तथान्वहम् ॥
2.26.m:
By one desiring heaven, long life, and prosperity, as well as for the appeasement of sin,
and by a mumukṣu, gifts must thus be given daily to brāhmaṇas.

2.26.s:
dīyamānaṃ tu yo mohād goviprāgnisureṣu ca /
nivārayati pāpātmā tiryagyoniṃ vrajet tu saḥ //
2.26.d:
दीयमानं तु यो मोहाद् गोविप्राग्निसुरेषु च ।
निवारयति पापात्मा तिर्यग्योनिं व्रजेत् तु सः ॥
2.26.m:
But that wicked person who, through delusion, obstructs [a gift]
being given to cows, brāhmaṇas, fire, or the gods, goes to an animal womb.

2.26.s:
yastu dravyārjanaṃ kṛtvā nārcayed brāhmaṇān surān /
sarvasvamapahṛtyainaṃ rājā rāṣṭrāt pravāsayet //
2.26.d:
यस्तु द्रव्यार्जनं कृत्वा नार्चयेद् ब्राह्मणान् सुरान् ।
सर्वस्वमपहृत्यैनं राजा राष्ट्रात् प्रवासयेत् ॥
2.26.m:
The king should confiscate all the wealth of him who, having acquired property,
does not honour brāhmaṇas and gods, and banish him from the realm.

2.26.s:
yastu durbhikṣavelāyāmannādyaṃ na prayacchati /
mriyamāṇeṣu vipreṣu brāhmaṇaḥ sa tu garhitaḥ //
2.26.d:
यस्तु दुर्भिक्षवेलायामन्नाद्यं न प्रयच्छति ।
म्रियमाणेषु विप्रेषु ब्राह्मणः स तु गर्हितः ॥
2.26.m:
But that brāhmaṇa who does not give food in a time of famine,
when vipras are dying, is truly contemptible.

2.26.s:
na tasmāt pratigṛhṇīyurna viśeyuśca tena hi /
aṅkayitvā svakād rāṣṭrāt taṃ rājā vipravāsayet //
2.26.d:
न तस्मात् प्रतिगृह्णीयुर्न विशेयुश्च तेन हि ।
अङ्कयित्वा स्वकाद् राष्ट्रात् तं राजा विप्रवासयेत् ॥
2.26.m:
One should not receive [anything] from him, nor should they enter [communion] with him;
having branded him, the king should banish him from his kingdom.

2.26.s:
yastvasadbhyo dadātīha svadravyaṃ dharmasādhanam /
sa pūrvābhyadhikaḥ pāpī narake pacyate naraḥ //
2.26.d:
यस्त्वसद्भ्यो ददातीह स्वद्रव्यं धर्मसाधनम् ।
स पूर्वाभ्यधिकः पापी नरके पच्यते नरः ॥
2.26.m:
He who gives here to unworthy men his own property, which is a means for [accomplishing] duty,
that sinful man, worse than the former, is cooked in hell.

2.26.s:
svādhyāyavanto ye viprā vidyāvanto jitendriyāḥ /
satyasaṃyamasaṃyuktāstebhyo dadyād dvijottamāḥ //
2.26.d:
स्वाध्यायवन्तो ये विप्रा विद्यावन्तो जितेन्द्रियाः ।
सत्यसंयमसंयुक्तास्तेभ्यो दद्याद् द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
2.26.m:
To those vipras who recite the sacred texts, possess knowledge, have mastered their senses,
and are endowed with truth and self-restraint, to them one should give, O best of the twice-born.

2.26.s:
subhuktamapi vidvāṃsaṃ dhārmikaṃ bhojayed dvijam /
na tu mūrkhamavṛttasthaṃ daśarātramupoṣitam //
2.26.d:
सुभुक्तमपि विद्वांसं धार्मिकं भोजयेद् द्विजम् ।
न तु मूर्खमवृत्तस्थं दशरात्रमुपोषितम् ॥
2.26.m:
One should feed a learned, virtuous twice-born even if he has already eaten well,
but never a fool who lives unrighteously, even if he has fasted for ten nights.

2.26.s:
sannikṛṣṭamatikramya śrotriyaṃ yaḥ prayacchati /
sa tena karmaṇā pāpī dahatyāsaptamaṃ kulam //
2.26.d:
सन्निकृष्टमतिक्रम्य श्रोत्रियं यः प्रयच्छति ।
स तेन कर्मणा पापी दहत्यासप्तमं कुलम् ॥
2.26.m:
He who passes over a nearby Vedic scholar and gives [elsewhere],
that sinner, by that deed, burns his family up to the seventh generation.

2.26.s:
yadisyādadhiko vipraḥ śīlavidyādibhiḥ svayam /
tasmai yatnena dātavyaṃ atikramyāpi sannidhim //
2.26.d:
यदिस्यादधिको विप्रः शीलविद्यादिभिः स्वयम् ।
तस्मै यत्नेन दातव्यं अतिक्रम्यापि सन्निधिम् ॥
2.26.m:
If a vipra should himself be superior in good conduct, learning, and the like,
to him [the gift] should be given with effort, even passing over someone nearby.

2.26.s:
yo 'rcitaṃ pratigṛhṇīyād dadyādarcitameva ca /
tāvubhau gacchataḥ svargaṃ narakaṃ tu viparyaye //
2.26.d:
यो ऽर्चितं प्रतिगृह्णीयाद् दद्यादर्चितमेव च ।
तावुभौ गच्छतः स्वर्गं नरकं तु विपर्यये ॥
2.26.m:
He who receives what is honored, and he who gives with honor,
both of them go to heaven; in the reverse case, however, to hell.

2.26.s:
na vāryapi prayaccheta nāstike haituke 'pi ca /
pāṣaṇḍeṣu ca sarveṣu nāvedavidi dharmavit //
2.26.d:
न वार्यपि प्रयच्छेत नास्तिके हैतुके ऽपि च ।
पाषण्डेषु च सर्वेषु नावेदविदि धर्मवित् ॥
2.26.m:
He who knows duty should not give even water to a non-believer, nor to a rationalist skeptic,
nor to any heretics, nor to one who does not know the Veda.

2.26.s:
apūpaṃ ca hiraṇyaṃ ca gāmaśvaṃ pṛthivīṃ tilān /
avidvān pratigṛhṇāno bhasmī bhavati kāṣṭhavat //
2.26.d:
अपूपं च हिरण्यं च गामश्वं पृथिवीं तिलान् ।
अविद्वान् प्रतिगृह्णानो भस्मी भवति काष्ठवत् ॥
2.26.m:
Accepting a cake, gold, a cow, a horse, land, or sesame seeds,
an unlearned man turns to ash like a piece of wood.

2.26.s:
dvijātibhyo dhanaṃ lipset praśastebhyo dvijottamaḥ /
api vā jātimātrebhyo na tu śūdrāt kathañcana //
2.26.d:
द्विजातिभ्यो धनं लिप्सेत् प्रशस्तेभ्यो द्विजोत्तमः ।
अपि वा जातिमात्रेभ्यो न तु शूद्रात् कथञ्चन ॥
2.26.m:
The best of the twice-born should desire wealth from commendable twice-born men,
or even from those twice-born merely by birth, but never from a śūdra.

2.26.s:
vṛttisaṅkocamanvicchenneheta dhanavistaram /
dhanalobhe prasaktastu brāhmaṇyādeva hīyate //
2.26.d:
वृत्तिसङ्कोचमन्विच्छेन्नेहेत धनविस्तरम् ।
धनलोभे प्रसक्तस्तु ब्राह्मण्यादेव हीयते ॥
2.26.m:
He should seek contraction of his livelihood; he should not desire expansion of wealth,
for one who is attached to the greed for wealth falls away from his brāhmaṇahood itself.

2.26.s:
vedānadhītya sakalān yajñāṃścāvāpya sarvaśaḥ /
na tāṃ gatimavāpnoti saṅkocād yāmavāpnuyāt //
2.26.d:
वेदानधीत्य सकलान् यज्ञांश्चावाप्य सर्वशः ।
न तां गतिमवाप्नोति सङ्कोचाद् यामवाप्नुयात् ॥
2.26.m:
Having studied all the Vedas and performed sacrifices everywhere,
one does not attain that goal which one would attain through contraction [of desires].

2.26.s:
pratigraharucirna syāt yātrārthaṃ tu samāharet /
sthityarthādadhikaṃ gṛhṇan brāhmaṇo yātyadhogatim //
2.26.d:
प्रतिग्रहरुचिर्न स्यात् यात्रार्थं तु समाहरेत् ।
स्थित्यर्थादधिकं गृह्णन् ब्राह्मणो यात्यधोगतिम् ॥
2.26.m:
He should not take pleasure in receiving gifts; he should gather only for the sake of sustenance;
taking more than is necessary for subsistence, a brāhmaṇa falls to a low state.

2.26.s:
yastu yācanako nityaṃ na sa svargasya bhājanam /
udvejayati bhūtāni yathā caurastathaiva saḥ //
2.26.d:
यस्तु याचनको नित्यं न स स्वर्गस्य भाजनम् ।
उद्वेजयति भूतानि यथा चौरस्तथैव सः ॥
2.26.m:
He who is constantly a beggar is not a recipient of heaven;
he distresses living beings, just as a thief does.

2.26.s:
gurūn bhṛtyāṃścojjihīrṣurarciṣyan devatātithīn /
sarvataḥ pratigṛhṇīyānna tu tṛpyet svayaṃ tataḥ //
2.26.d:
गुरून् भृत्यांश्चोज्जिहीर्षुरर्चिष्यन् देवतातिथीन् ।
सर्वतः प्रतिगृह्णीयान्न तु तृप्येत् स्वयं ततः ॥
2.26.m:
Desiring to support gurus and servants, and intending to honor gods and guests,
he may accept from all; but he should not himself be satisfied thereby.

2.26.s:
evaṃ gṛhastho yuktātmā devatātithipūjakaḥ /
vartamānaḥ saṃyātātmā yāti tat paramaṃ padam //
2.26.d:
एवं गृहस्थो युक्तात्मा देवतातिथिपूजकः ।
वर्तमानः संयातात्मा याति तत् परमं पदम् ॥
2.26.m:
Thus a householder, disciplined, worshipping deities and guests,
conducting himself with a controlled mind, reaches that supreme state.

2.26.s:
putre nidhāya vā sarvaṃ gatvāraṇyaṃ tu tattvavit /
ekākī vicarennityamudāsīnaḥ samāhitaḥ //
2.26.d:
पुत्रे निधाय वा सर्वं गत्वारण्यं तु तत्त्ववित् ।
एकाकी विचरेन्नित्यमुदासीनः समाहितः ॥
2.26.m:
Or, having placed everything upon his son and gone to the forest, knowing the true reality,
he should wander continually alone, indifferent, and concentrated in mind.

2.26.s:
eṣa vaḥ kathito dharmo gṛhasthānāṃ dvijottamāḥ /
jñātvānutiṣṭhenniyataṃ tathānuṣṭhāpayed dvijān //
2.26.d:
एष वः कथितो धर्मो गृहस्थानां द्विजोत्तमाः ।
ज्ञात्वानुतिष्ठेन्नियतं तथानुष्ठापयेद् द्विजान् ॥
2.26.m:
This duty of householders has been declared to you, O best of the twice-born;
having known it, one should perform it constantly, and likewise cause the twice-born to perform it.

2.26.s:
iti devamanādimekamīśaṃ
gṛhadharmeṇa samarcayedajastram /
samatītya sa sarvabhūtayoniṃ
prakṛtiṃ yāti paraṃ na yāti janma //
iti śrīkūrmapurāṇe ṣaṭsāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāmuparivibhāge ṣaḍviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.26.d:
इति देवमनादिमेकमीशं
गृहधर्मेण समर्चयेदजस्त्रम् ।
समतीत्य स सर्वभूतयोनिं
प्रकृतिं याति परं न याति जन्म ॥
इति श्रीकूर्मपुराणे षट्साहस्त्र्यां संहितायामुपरिविभागे षड्विंशो ऽध्यायः
2.26.m:
Thus one should incessantly worship the one beginningless God, the Lord,
through the duty of the householder;
having transcended primordial matter, the womb of all beings, he reaches the Supreme and does not go to [re]birth.

Thus ends the twenty-sixth chapter in the latter section of the compilation of six thousand verses in the glorious Kūrma Purāṇa.

2.27.s:
vyāsa uvāca
evaṃ gṛhāśrame sthitvā dvitīyaṃ bhāgamāyuṣaḥ /
vānaprasthāśramaṃ gacchet sadāraḥ sāgnireva ca //
nikṣipya bhāryāṃ putreṣu gacched vanamathāpi vā /
dṛṣṭvāpatyasya cāpatyaṃ jarjarīkṛtavigrahaḥ //
2.27.d:
व्यास उवाच
एवं गृहाश्रमे स्थित्वा द्वितीयं भागमायुषः ।
वानप्रस्थाश्रमं गच्छेत् सदारः साग्निरेव च ॥
निक्षिप्य भार्यां पुत्रेषु गच्छेद् वनमथापि वा ।
दृष्ट्वापत्यस्य चापत्यं जर्जरीकृतविग्रहः ॥
2.27.m:
Vyāsa said:
Having thus lived in the stage of a householder for the second part of one's life,
one should enter the stage of a forest hermit along with his wife and together with his sacred fire;
or, having entrusted his wife to his sons, he may go to the forest,
having seen the child of his child, with his body worn out by old age.

2.27.s:
śuklapakṣasya pūrvāhne praśaste cottarāyaṇe /
gatvāraṇyaṃ niyamavāṃstapaḥ kuryāt samāhitaḥ //
2.27.d:
शुक्लपक्षस्य पूर्वाह्ने प्रशस्ते चोत्तरायणे ।
गत्वारण्यं नियमवांस्तपः कुर्यात् समाहितः ॥
2.27.m:
In the forenoon of the bright fortnight, during the auspicious northern course of the sun,
having gone to the forest, observing vows, he should practice austerity, concentrated in mind.

2.27.s:
phalamūlāni pūtāni nityamāhāramāharet /
yatāhāro bhavet tena pūjayet pitṛdevatāḥ //
2.27.d:
फलमूलानि पूतानि नित्यमाहारमाहरेत् ।
यताहारो भवेत् तेन पूजयेत् पितृदेवताः ॥
2.27.m:
He should always gather pure fruits and roots for food;
he should be restrained in his food, and with that he should worship the ancestors and the gods.

2.27.s:
pūjayitvātithiṃ nityaṃ snātvā cābhyarcayet surān /
gṛhādāhṛtya cāśnīyādaṣṭau grāsān samāhitaḥ //
2.27.d:
पूजयित्वातिथिं नित्यं स्नात्वा चाभ्यर्चयेत् सुरान् ।
गृहादाहृत्य चाश्नीयादष्टौ ग्रासान् समाहितः ॥
2.27.m:
Having always honored a guest and having bathed, he should worship the gods;
and having brought [food] from a house, he should eat eight mouthfuls, collected in mind.

2.27.s:
jaṭāśca bibhṛyānnityaṃ nakharomāṇi notsṛjet /
svādhyāyaṃ sarvadā kuryānniyacched vācamanyataḥ //
2.27.d:
जटाश्च बिभृयान्नित्यं नखरोमाणि नोत्सृजेत् ।
स्वाध्यायं सर्वदा कुर्यान्नियच्छेद् वाचमन्यतः ॥
2.27.m:
He should constantly wear matted hair and should not cut his nails and hair;
he should always engage in recitation of the sacred texts and restrain his speech from everything else.

2.27.s:
agnihotraṃ ca juhuyāt pañcayajñān samācaret /
munyannaiṃrvividhairmedhyaiḥ śākamūlaphalena vā //
2.27.d:
अग्निहोत्रं च जुहुयात् पञ्चयज्ञान् समाचरेत् ।
मुन्यन्नैंर्विविधैर्मेध्यैः शाकमूलफलेन वा ॥
2.27.m:
He should perform the daily fire offering and carry out the five daily sacrifices,
with various pure hermit foods, or with vegetables, roots, and fruits.

2.27.s:
cīravāsā bhavennityaṃ snāyāt triṣavaṇaṃ śuciḥ /
sarvabhūtānukampī syāt pratigrahavivarjitaḥ //
2.27.d:
चीरवासा भवेन्नित्यं स्नायात् त्रिषवणं शुचिः ।
सर्वभूतानुकम्पी स्यात् प्रतिग्रहविवर्जितः ॥
2.27.m:
He should always wear rags or bark, bathe at the three junctures of the day, pure;
he should be compassionate to all beings, and free from accepting gifts.

2.27.s:
darśena paurṇamāsena yajet niyataṃ dvijaḥ /
ṛkṣeṣvāgrayaṇe caiva cāturmāsyāni cāharet /
uttarāyaṇaṃ ca kramaśo dakṣasyāyanameva ca //
2.27.d:
दर्शेन पौर्णमासेन यजेत् नियतं द्विजः ।
ऋक्षेष्वाग्रयणे चैव चातुर्मास्यानि चाहरेत् ।
उत्तरायणं च क्रमशो दक्षस्यायनमेव च ॥
2.27.m:
A twice-born should regularly sacrifice with the new-moon and full-moon rites,
and he should perform the sacrifice of first fruits under the asterisms, and the four-month rites,
and gradually during the northern course and the southern course of the sun.

2.27.s:
vāsantaiḥ śāradairmedhyairmunyannaiḥ svayamāhṛtaiḥ /
puroḍāśāṃścarūṃścaiva vidhivannirvapet pṛthak //
2.27.d:
वासन्तैः शारदैर्मेध्यैर्मुन्यन्नैः स्वयमाहृतैः ।
पुरोडाशांश्चरूंश्चैव विधिवन्निर्वपेत् पृथक् ॥
2.27.m:
With pure hermit-foods of spring and autumn gathered by himself,
he should separately offer sacrificial cakes and boiled rice offerings according to the rule.

2.27.s:
devatābhyaśca tad hutvā vanyaṃ medhyataraṃ haviḥ /
śeṣaṃ samupabhuñjīta lavaṇaṃ ca svayaṃ kṛtam //
2.27.d:
देवताभ्यश्च तद् हुत्वा वन्यं मेध्यतरं हविः ।
शेषं समुपभुञ्जीत लवणं च स्वयं कृतम् ॥
2.27.m:
And having offered that most pure wild oblation to the deities,
he should consume the remainder, along with salt made by himself.

2.27.s:
varjayenmadhumāṃsāni bhaumāni kavakāni ca /
bhūstṛṇaṃ śigrukaṃ caiva śleṣmātakaphalāni ca //
2.27.d:
वर्जयेन्मधुमांसानि भौमानि कवकानि च ।
भूस्तृणं शिग्रुकं चैव श्लेष्मातकफलानि च ॥
2.27.m:
He should avoid honey and meat, mushrooms that grow from the earth,
fragrant grass, moringa, and śleṣmātaka fruits.

2.27.s:
na phālakṛṣṭamaśnīyādutsṛṣṭamapi kenacit /
na grāmajātānyārto 'pi puṣpāṇi ca phalāni ca //
2.27.d:
न फालकृष्टमश्नीयादुत्सृष्टमपि केनचित् ।
न ग्रामजातान्यार्तो ऽपि पुष्पाणि च फलानि च ॥
2.27.m:
He should not eat what has been plowed by a plowshare, even if discarded by someone,
nor fruits and flowers that have grown in a village, even if he is distressed.

2.27.s:
śrāvaṇenaiva vidhinā vahniṃ paricaret sadā /
na druhyet sarvabhūtāni nirdvandvo nirbhayo bhavet //
2.27.d:
श्रावणेनैव विधिना वह्निं परिचरेत् सदा ।
न द्रुह्येत् सर्वभूतानि निर्द्वन्द्वो निर्भयो भवेत् ॥
2.27.m:
He should constantly attend to the fire according to the Śrāvaṇa rule;
he should not injure any beings, and he should be free from dualities and free from fear.

2.27.s:
na naktaṃ kiñcidaśnīyād rātrau dhyānaparo bhavet /
jitendriyo jitakrodhastattvajñānavicintakaḥ /
brahmacārī bhavennityaṃ na patnīmapi saṃśrayet //
2.27.d:
न नक्तं किञ्चिदश्नीयाद् रात्रौ ध्यानपरो भवेत् ।
जितेन्द्रियो जितक्रोधस्तत्त्वज्ञानविचिन्तकः ।
ब्रह्मचारी भवेन्नित्यं न पत्नीमपि संश्रयेत् ॥

2.27.s:
yastu patnyā vanaṃ gatvā maithunaṃ kāmataścaret /
tad vrataṃ tasya lupyeta prāyaścittīyate dvijaḥ //
2.27.d:
यस्तु पत्न्या वनं गत्वा मैथुनं कामतश्चरेत् ।
तद् व्रतं तस्य लुप्येत प्रायश्चित्तीयते द्विजः ॥
2.27.m:
If one who has gone to the forest with his wife should engage in sexual intercourse through desire,
that vow of his would be broken, and the twice-born must perform an expiation.

2.27.s:
tatra yo jāyate garbho na saṃspṛśyo dvijātibhiḥ /
na hi vede 'dhikāro 'sya tadvaṃśepyevameva hi //
2.27.d:
तत्र यो जायते गर्भो न संस्पृश्यो द्विजातिभिः ।
न हि वेदे ऽधिकारो ऽस्य तद्वंशेप्येवमेव हि ॥
2.27.m:
The child that is born there is not to be touched by the twice-born;
for he has no right to the Veda, and the same holds true for his lineage.

2.27.s:
adhaḥ śayīta satataṃ sāvitrījāpyatatparaḥ /
śaraṇyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ saṃvibhāgaparaḥ sadā //
2.27.d:
अधः शयीत सततं सावित्रीजाप्यतत्परः ।
शरण्यः सर्वभूतानां संविभागपरः सदा ॥
2.27.m:
He should constantly sleep on the ground, devoted to the chanting of the Sāvitrī,
a refuge for all beings, always intent on sharing [with others].

2.27.s:
parivādaṃ mṛṣāvādaṃ nidrālasyaṃ vivarjayet /
ekāgniraniketaḥ syāt prokṣitāṃ bhūmimāśrayet //
2.27.d:
परिवादं मृषावादं निद्रालस्यं विवर्जयेत् ।
एकाग्निरनिकेतः स्यात् प्रोक्षितां भूमिमाश्रयेत् ॥
2.27.m:
He should avoid slander, falsehood, sleep, and laziness;
he should maintain a single fire, be homeless, and resort to sprinkled ground.

2.27.s:
mṛgaiḥ saha cared vāsaṃ taiḥ sahaiva ca saṃvaset /
śilāyāṃ śarkarāyāṃ vā śayīta susamāhitaḥ //
2.27.d:
मृगैः सह चरेद् वासं तैः सहैव च संवसेत् ।
शिलायां शर्करायां वा शयीत सुसमाहितः ॥
2.27.m:
He should move about dwelling with deer, and he should dwell together with them;
he should sleep on a flat rock or gravel, perfectly collected in mind.

2.27.s:
sadyaḥ prakṣālako vā syānmāsasaṃcayiko 'pi vā /
ṣaṇmāsanicayo vā syāt samānicaya eva vā //
2.27.d:
सद्यः प्रक्षालको वा स्यान्माससंचयिको ऽपि वा ।
षण्मासनिचयो वा स्यात् समानिचय एव वा ॥
2.27.m:
He may wash [his food] immediately, or store for a month,
or he may store for six months, or store for a year.

2.27.s:
tyajedāśvayuje māsi saṃpannaṃ pūrvasaṃcitam /
jīrṇāni caiva vāsāṃsi śākamūlaphalāni ca //
2.27.d:
त्यजेदाश्वयुजे मासि संपन्नं पूर्वसंचितम् ।
जीर्णानि चैव वासांसि शाकमूलफलानि च ॥
2.27.m:
In the month of Āśvayuja, he should discard what was previously collected and accumulated,
as well as worn-out clothes, vegetables, roots, and fruits.

2.27.s:
dantolūkhaliko vāsyāt kāpotīṃ vṛttimāśrayet /
aśmakuṭṭo bhaved vāpi kālapakvabhugeva vā //
2.27.d:
दन्तोलूखलिको वास्यात् कापोतीं वृत्तिमाश्रयेत् ।
अश्मकुट्टो भवेद् वापि कालपक्वभुगेव वा ॥
2.27.m:
He may use his teeth as a mortar, or adopt the lifestyle of pigeons,
or he may be a pounder with stones, or eat only what is ripened by time.

2.27.s:
naktaṃ cānna samaśnīyād divā cāhṛtya śaktitaḥ /
caturthakāliko vā syāt syādvāpyaṣṭamakālikaḥ //
2.27.d:
नक्तं चान्न समश्नीयाद् दिवा चाहृत्य शक्तितः ।
चतुर्थकालिको वा स्यात् स्याद्वाप्यष्टमकालिकः ॥
2.27.m:
He should eat food at night, having gathered it during the day according to his ability;
or he may eat at every fourth meal-time, or even at every eighth meal-time.

2.27.s:
cāndrāyaṇavidhānairvā śukle kṛṣṇe ca vartayet /
pakṣe pakṣe samaśnīyād yavāgūṃ kvathitāṃ sakṛt //
2.27.d:
चान्द्रायणविधानैर्वा शुक्ले कृष्णे च वर्तयेत् ।
पक्षे पक्षे समश्नीयाद् यवागूं क्वथितां सकृत् ॥
2.27.m:
Or he may subsist according to the rules of the Cāndrāyaṇa penance during the bright and dark fortnights;
he may eat boiled barley gruel once in each fortnight.

2.27.s:
puṣpamūlaphalairvāpi kevalairvartayet sadā /
svābhāvikaiḥ svayaṃ śīrṇairvaikhānasamate sthitaḥ //
2.27.d:
पुष्पमूलफलैर्वापि केवलैर्वर्तयेत् सदा ।
स्वाभाविकैः स्वयं शीर्णैर्वैखानसमते स्थितः ॥
2.27.m:
He may also sustain himself always on flowers, roots, and fruits alone,
naturally fallen of their own accord, adhering to the Vaikhānasa doctrine.

2.27.s:
bhūmau vā parivarteta tiṣṭhed vā prapadairdinam /
sthānāsanābhyāṃ viharenna kvacid dhairyamutsṛjet //
2.27.d:
भूमौ वा परिवर्तेत तिष्ठेद् वा प्रपदैर्दिनम् ।
स्थानासनाभ्यां विहरेन्न क्वचिद् धैर्यमुत्सृजेत् ॥
2.27.m:
He may roll upon the earth, or remain on the tips of his feet for a day;
he should pass his time standing and sitting, and never abandon fortitude.

2.27.s:
grīṣme pañcatapāśca syād varṣāsvabhrāvakāśakaḥ /
ārdravāsāstu hemante kramaśo vardhayaṃstapaḥ //
2.27.d:
ग्रीष्मे पञ्चतपाश्च स्याद् वर्षास्वभ्रावकाशकः ।
आर्द्रवासास्तु हेमन्ते क्रमशो वर्धयंस्तपः ॥
2.27.m:
In summer he should practice the five fires, in the rainy seasons remain exposed to the clouds,
and in the cold season wear wet clothes, gradually increasing his ascetic heat.

2.27.s:
upaspṛśya triṣavaṇaṃ pitṛdevāṃśca tarpayet /
ekapādena tiṣṭheta marīcīn vā pibet tadā //
2.27.d:
उपस्पृश्य त्रिषवणं पितृदेवांश्च तर्पयेत् ।
एकपादेन तिष्ठेत मरीचीन् वा पिबेत् तदा ॥
2.27.m:
