Having bathed at the three junctures of the day, he should offer libations to the ancestors and gods;
he should stand on one foot, or then drink rays [of the sun].

2.27.s:
pañcāgnirdhūmapo vā syāduṣmapaḥ somapo 'pi vā /
payaḥ pibecchuklapakṣe kṛṣṇāpakṣe tu gomayam /
śīrṇaparṇāśano vā syāt kṛcchrair vā vartayet sadā //
2.27.d:
पञ्चाग्निर्धूमपो वा स्यादुष्मपः सोमपो ऽपि वा ।
पयः पिबेच्छुक्लपक्षे कृष्णापक्षे तु गोमयम् ।
शीर्णपर्णाशनो वा स्यात् कृच्छ्रैर् वा वर्तयेत् सदा ॥

2.27.s:
yogābhyāsarataśca syād rudrādhyāyī bhavet sadā /
atharvaśiraso 'dhyetā vedāntābhyāsatatparaḥ //
2.27.d:
योगाभ्यासरतश्च स्याद् रुद्राध्यायी भवेत् सदा ।
अथर्वशिरसो ऽध्येता वेदान्ताभ्यासतत्परः ॥
2.27.m:
He should be devoted to the practice of yoga and always recite the Śatarudrīya;
he should study the Atharvaśiras Upaniṣad, devoted to the practice of Vedānta.

2.27.s:
yamān seveta satataṃ niyamāṃścāpyatandritaḥ /
kṛṣṇājinī sottarīyaḥ śuklayajñopavītavān //
2.27.d:
यमान् सेवेत सततं नियमांश्चाप्यतन्द्रितः ।
कृष्णाजिनी सोत्तरीयः शुक्लयज्ञोपवीतवान् ॥
2.27.m:
He should constantly observe the restraints and observances without sloth,
wearing a black antelope skin and an upper garment, possessing a white sacrificial thread.

2.27.s:
atha cāgnīn samāropya svātmani dhyānatatparaḥ /
anagniraniketaḥ syānmunirmokṣaparo bhavet //
2.27.d:
अथ चाग्नीन् समारोप्य स्वात्मनि ध्यानतत्परः ।
अनग्निरनिकेतः स्यान्मुनिर्मोक्षपरो भवेत् ॥
2.27.m:
Then, having deposited the fires within himself, intent upon meditation,
fireless and homeless, a silent sage, he should become intent upon liberation.

2.27.s:
tāpaseṣveva vipreṣu yātrikaṃ bhaikṣamāharet /
gṛhamedhiṣu cānyeṣu dvijeṣu vanavāsiṣu //
2.27.d:
तापसेष्वेव विप्रेषु यात्रिकं भैक्षमाहरेत् ।
गृहमेधिषु चान्येषु द्विजेषु वनवासिषु ॥
2.27.m:
He should collect only as much alms as is needed for sustenance among ascetic brāhmaṇas,
householders, and other twice-born forest dwellers.

2.27.s:
grāmādāhṛtya vāśnīyādaṣṭau grāsān vane vasan /
pratigṛhya puṭenaiva pāṇinā śakalena vā //
2.27.d:
ग्रामादाहृत्य वाश्नीयादष्टौ ग्रासान् वने वसन् ।
प्रतिगृह्य पुटेनैव पाणिना शकलेन वा ॥
2.27.m:
Or, dwelling in the forest, he should eat eight mouthfuls brought from a village,
receiving them in a leaf-cup, in his bare hand, or in an earthen potsherd.

2.27.s:
vividhāścopaniṣada ātmasaṃsiddhaye japet /
vidyāviśeṣān sāvitrīṃ rudrādhyāyaṃ tathaiva ca //
2.27.d:
विविधाश्चोपनिषद आत्मसंसिद्धये जपेत् ।
विद्याविशेषान् सावित्रीं रुद्राध्यायं तथैव च ॥
2.27.m:
For the perfection of the Self he should softly recite various Upaniṣads,
special forms of sacred knowledge, the Sāvitrī mantra, and likewise the Śatarudrīya.

2.27.s:
mahāprāsthānikaṃ cāsau kuryādanaśanaṃ tu vā /
agnipraveśamanyad vā brarhmārpaṇavidhau sthitaḥ //
2.27.d:
महाप्रास्थानिकं चासौ कुर्यादनशनं तु वा ।
अग्निप्रवेशमन्यद् वा ब्रर्ह्मार्पणविधौ स्थितः ॥
2.27.m:
And he may undertake the Great Departure, or fasting unto death,
or entry into fire, or another [death], established in the rite of dedicating all to Brahman.

2.27.s:
yastu samyagimamāśramaṃ śivaṃ
saṃśrayedaśivapuñjanāśanam /
tāpasaḥ sa paramaiśvaraṃ padaṃ
yāti yatra jagato 'sya saṃsthitiḥ //
iti śrīkūrmapurāṇe ṣaṭsāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāmuparivibhāge saptaviśo 'dhyāya
2.27.d:
यस्तु सम्यगिममाश्रमं शिवं
संश्रयेदशिवपुञ्जनाशनम् ।
तापसः स परमैश्वरं पदं
याति यत्र जगतो ऽस्य संस्थितिः ॥
इति श्रीकूर्मपुराणे षट्साहस्त्र्यां संहितायामुपरिविभागे सप्तविशो ऽध्याय
2.27.m:
The ascetic who properly resorts to this auspicious stage of life,
which destroys the mass of inauspiciousness,
goes to the supreme state of the Lord,
wherein lies the foundation of this world.

Thus ends the twenty-seventh chapter in the latter section of the compilation of six thousand verses in the glorious Kūrma Purāṇa.

2.28.s:
vyāsa uvāca
evaṃ vanāśrame sthitvā tṛtīyaṃ bhāgamāyuṣaḥ /
caturthamāyuṣo bhāgaṃ saṃnyāsena nayet kramāt //
2.28.d:
व्यास उवाच
एवं वनाश्रमे स्थित्वा तृतीयं भागमायुषः ।
चतुर्थमायुषो भागं संन्यासेन नयेत् क्रमात् ॥
2.28.m:
Vyāsa said:
Having thus lived in the forest stage of life for the third portion of one's lifespan,
one should duly spend the fourth portion of life in renunciation.

2.28.s:
agnīnātmanī saṃsthāpya dvijaḥ pravrajito bhavet /
yogābhyāsarataḥ śānto brahmavidyāparāyaṇaḥ //
2.28.d:
अग्नीनात्मनी संस्थाप्य द्विजः प्रव्रजितो भवेत् ।
योगाभ्यासरतः शान्तो ब्रह्मविद्यापरायणः ॥
2.28.m:
Having placed the sacred fires within himself, a twice-born should become a mendicant,
devoted to the practice of yoga, tranquil, intent upon the knowledge of Brahman.

2.28.s:
yadā manasi saṃjātaṃ vaitṛṣṇyaṃ sarvavastuṣu /
tadā saṃnyāsamicchecca patitaḥ syād viparyaye //
2.28.d:
यदा मनसि संजातं वैतृष्ण्यं सर्ववस्तुषु ।
तदा संन्यासमिच्छेच्च पतितः स्याद् विपर्यये ॥
2.28.m:
When freedom from thirst for all things has arisen in the mind,
then one may desire renunciation; if it is otherwise, he falls.

2.28.s:
prājāpatyāṃ nirūpyeṣṭimāgneyīmathavā punaḥ /
dāntaḥ pakvakaṣāyo 'sau brahmāśramamupāśrayet //
2.28.d:
प्राजापत्यां निरूप्येष्टिमाग्नेयीमथवा पुनः ।
दान्तः पक्वकषायो ऽसौ ब्रह्माश्रममुपाश्रयेत् ॥
2.28.m:
Having performed the Prājāpatya sacrifice, or else the Āgneya sacrifice,
self-controlled, his impurities burned away, he should resort to the stage of life devoted to Brahman.

2.28.s:
jñānasaṃnyāsinaḥ kecid vedasaṃnyāsinaḥ pare /
karmasaṃnyāsinastvanye trividhāḥ parikīrtitāḥ //
2.28.d:
ज्ञानसंन्यासिनः केचिद् वेदसंन्यासिनः परे ।
कर्मसंन्यासिनस्त्वन्ये त्रिविधाः परिकीर्तिताः ॥
2.28.m:
Some are renunciants through knowledge; others are renunciants through the Veda;
and others are renunciants through ritual action—three kinds are proclaimed.

2.28.s:
yaḥ sarvasaṅganirmukto nirdvandvaścaiva nirbhayaḥ /
procyate jñānasaṃnyāsī svātmanyeva vyavasthitaḥ //
2.28.d:
यः सर्वसङ्गनिर्मुक्तो निर्द्वन्द्वश्चैव निर्भयः ।
प्रोच्यते ज्ञानसंन्यासी स्वात्मन्येव व्यवस्थितः ॥
2.28.m:
He who is completely freed from all attachment, beyond the dualities, and fearless,
established in his own self alone, is called a renunciant through knowledge.

2.28.s:
vedamevābhyasennityaṃ nirāśī niṣparigrahaḥ /
procyate vedasaṃnyāsī mumukṣurvijitendriyaḥ //
2.28.d:
वेदमेवाभ्यसेन्नित्यं निराशी निष्परिग्रहः ।
प्रोच्यते वेदसंन्यासी मुमुक्षुर्विजितेन्द्रियः ॥
2.28.m:
He who continually studies only the Veda, devoid of desire, without possessions,
a mumukṣu whose senses are conquered, is called a renunciant through the Veda.

2.28.s:
yastvagnīnātmasātkṛtvā brahmārpaṇaparo dvijaḥ /
jñeyaḥ sa karmasaṃnyāsī mahāyajñaparāyaṇaḥ //
2.28.d:
यस्त्वग्नीनात्मसात्कृत्वा ब्रह्मार्पणपरो द्विजः ।
ज्ञेयः स कर्मसंन्यासी महायज्ञपरायणः ॥
2.28.m:
The twice-born who, having internalized the fires, is intent on dedicating all to Brahman
and devoted to the great sacrifices, should be known as a renunciant through ritual action.

2.28.s:
trayāṇāmapi caiteṣāṃ jñānī tvabhyadhiko mataḥ /
na tasya vidyate kāryaṃ na liṅgaṃ vā vipaścitaḥ //
2.28.d:
त्रयाणामपि चैतेषां ज्ञानी त्वभ्यधिको मतः ।
न तस्य विद्यते कार्यं न लिङ्गं वा विपश्चितः ॥
2.28.m:
Yet among these three, the possessor of knowledge is considered pre-eminent;
for that wise one there is no obligation, nor any external emblem.

2.28.s:
nirmamo nirbhayaḥ śānto nirdvandvaḥ parṇabhojanaḥ /
jīrṇakaupīnavāsāḥ syānnagno vā dhyānatatparaḥ //
2.28.d:
निर्ममो निर्भयः शान्तो निर्द्वन्द्वः पर्णभोजनः ।
जीर्णकौपीनवासाः स्यान्नग्नो वा ध्यानतत्परः ॥
2.28.m:
Free from mineness, fearless, tranquil, beyond the dualities, eating leaves,
wearing a worn loincloth, or naked, he should be intent on meditation.

2.28.s:
brahmacārī mitāhāro grāmādannaṃ samāharet /
adhyātmamatirāsīta nirapekṣo nirāmiṣaḥ //
2.28.d:
ब्रह्मचारी मिताहारो ग्रामादन्नं समाहरेत् ।
अध्यात्ममतिरासीत निरपेक्षो निरामिषः ॥
2.28.m:
Celibate, eating measured food, he should collect alms-food from a village;
he should sit with his mind fixed on the Self, free from expectation and free from desire.

2.28.s:
ātmanaiva sahāyena sukhārthaṃ vicarediha /
nābhinandeta maraṇaṃ nābhinandeta jīvitam //
2.28.d:
आत्मनैव सहायेन सुखार्थं विचरेदिह ।
नाभिनन्देत मरणं नाभिनन्देत जीवितम् ॥
2.28.m:
He should wander in this world with only himself as his companion for the sake of happiness;
he should not rejoice at death, nor should he rejoice at life.

2.28.s:
kālameva pratīkṣeta nideśaṃ bhṛtako yathā /
nādhyetavyaṃ na vaktavyaṃ śrotavyaṃ na kadācana /
evaṃ jñātvā paro yogī brahmabhūyāya kalpate //
2.28.d:
कालमेव प्रतीक्षेत निदेशं भृतको यथा ।
नाध्येतव्यं न वक्तव्यं श्रोतव्यं न कदाचन ।
एवं ज्ञात्वा परो योगी ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ॥

2.28.s:
ekavāsāthavā vidvān kaupīnācchādanastathā /
muṇḍī śikhī vātha bhavet tridaṇḍī niṣparigrahaḥ /
kāṣāyavāsāḥ satataṃ dhyānayogaparāyaṇaḥ //
2.28.d:
एकवासाथवा विद्वान् कौपीनाच्छादनस्तथा ।
मुण्डी शिखी वाथ भवेत् त्रिदण्डी निष्परिग्रहः ।
काषायवासाः सततं ध्यानयोगपरायणः ॥

2.28.s:
grāmānte vṛkṣamūle vā vased devālaye 'pi vā /
samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca tathā mānāpamānayoḥ /
bhaikṣyeṇa vartayennityaṃ naikānnādī bhavet kvacit //
2.28.d:
ग्रामान्ते वृक्षमूले वा वसेद् देवालये ऽपि वा ।
समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च तथा मानापमानयोः ।
भैक्ष्येण वर्तयेन्नित्यं नैकान्नादी भवेत् क्वचित् ॥

2.28.s:
yastu mohena vālasyādekānnādī bhaved yatiḥ /
na tasya niṣkṛtiḥ kācid dharmaśāstreṣu kathyate //
2.28.d:
यस्तु मोहेन वालस्यादेकान्नादी भवेद् यतिः ।
न तस्य निष्कृतिः काचिद् धर्मशास्त्रेषु कथ्यते ॥
2.28.m:
The ascetic who, through delusion or laziness, eats food from a single household,
for him no expiation is stated in the treatises on duty.

2.28.s:
rāgadveṣavimuktātmā samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanaḥ /
prāṇihaṃsānivṛttaśca maunī syāt sarvanispṛhaḥ //
2.28.d:
रागद्वेषविमुक्तात्मा समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः ।
प्राणिहंसानिवृत्तश्च मौनी स्यात् सर्वनिस्पृहः ॥
2.28.m:
His self freed from passion and hatred, regarding a clod of earth, a stone, and gold as equal,
ceasing from harming living beings, he should remain silent and free from all craving.

2.28.s:
dṛṣṭipūtaṃ nyaset pādaṃ vastrapūtaṃ jalaṃ pibet /
satyapūtāṃ vaded vāṇīṃ manaḥ pūtaṃ samācaret //
2.28.d:
दृष्टिपूतं न्यसेत् पादं वस्त्रपूतं जलं पिबेत् ।
सत्यपूतां वदेद् वाणीं मनः पूतं समाचरेत् ॥
2.28.m:
He should set down his foot purified by sight; he should drink water purified by cloth;
he should speak speech purified by truth; he should perform what is purified by the mind.

2.28.s:
naikatra nivased deśe varṣābhyo 'nyatra bhikṣukaḥ /
snānaśaucarato nityaṃ kamaṇḍalukaraḥ śuciḥ //
2.28.d:
नैकत्र निवसेद् देशे वर्षाभ्यो ऽन्यत्र भिक्षुकः ।
स्नानशौचरतो नित्यं कमण्डलुकरः शुचिः ॥
2.28.m:
The mendicant should not dwell in one place except during the rainy season;
always devoted to bathing and purification, holding a water-pot in his hand, pure.

2.28.s:
brahmacaryarato nityaṃ vanavāsarato bhavet /
mokṣaśāstreṣu nirato brahmasūtrī jitendriyaḥ //
2.28.d:
ब्रह्मचर्यरतो नित्यं वनवासरतो भवेत् ।
मोक्षशास्त्रेषु निरतो ब्रह्मसूत्री जितेन्द्रियः ॥
2.28.m:
Always devoted to celibacy, he should be fond of dwelling in the forest,
devoted to the treatises on liberation, wearing the sacred thread of Brahman, with senses conquered.

2.28.s:
dambhāhaṅkāranirmukto nindāpaiśunyavarjitaḥ /
ātmajñānaguṇopeto yatirmokṣamavāpnuyāt //
2.28.d:
दम्भाहङ्कारनिर्मुक्तो निन्दापैशुन्यवर्जितः ।
आत्मज्ञानगुणोपेतो यतिर्मोक्षमवाप्नुयात् ॥
2.28.m:
Freed from deceit and egoism, free from censure and slander,
endowed with the virtues of knowledge of the Self, the ascetic will attain liberation.

2.28.s:
abhyaset satataṃ vedaṃ praṇavākhyaṃ sanātanam /
snātvācamya vidhānena śucirdevālayādiṣu //
2.28.d:
अभ्यसेत् सततं वेदं प्रणवाख्यं सनातनम् ।
स्नात्वाचम्य विधानेन शुचिर्देवालयादिषु ॥
2.28.m:
He should constantly study the eternal Veda named the Praṇava,
having bathed and sipped water according to the rule, pure in temples of the gods and the like.

2.28.s:
yajñopavītī śāntātmā kuśapāṇiḥ samāhitaḥ /
dhautakāṣāyavasano bhasmacchannatanūrahaḥ //
2.28.d:
यज्ञोपवीती शान्तात्मा कुशपाणिः समाहितः ।
धौतकाषायवसनो भस्मच्छन्नतनूरहः ॥
2.28.m:
Wearing a sacrificial thread, tranquil-minded, holding kuśa grass in hand, collected in mind,
wearing washed ochre robes, his bodily hair covered in ashes.

2.28.s:
adhiyajñaṃ brahma japedādhidaivikameva ca /
ādhyātmikaṃ ca satataṃ vedāntābhihitaṃ ca yat //
2.28.d:
अधियज्ञं ब्रह्म जपेदाधिदैविकमेव च ।
आध्यात्मिकं च सततं वेदान्ताभिहितं च यत् ॥
2.28.m:
He should constantly recite Brahman relating to sacrifice, relating to the divinities,
and relating to the inner Self, which is taught in the Vedānta.

2.28.s:
putreṣu vātha nivasan brahmacārī yatirmuniḥ /
vedamevābhyasennityaṃ sa yāti paramāṃ gatim //
2.28.d:
पुत्रेषु वाथ निवसन् ब्रह्मचारी यतिर्मुनिः ।
वेदमेवाभ्यसेन्नित्यं स याति परमां गतिम् ॥
2.28.m:
Or dwelling among his sons as a celibate ascetic sage,
he should continually study the Veda alone; he goes to the supreme state.

2.28.s:
ahiṃsā satyamasteyaṃ brahmacaryaṃ tapaḥ param /
kṣamā dayā ca satoṣo vratānyasya viśeṣataḥ //
2.28.d:
अहिंसा सत्यमस्तेयं ब्रह्मचर्यं तपः परम् ।
क्षमा दया च सतोषो व्रतान्यस्य विशेषतः ॥
2.28.m:
Non-violence, truthfulness, non-stealing, celibacy, supreme austerity,
forbearance, compassion, and contentment are especially his observances.

2.28.s:
vedāntajñānaniṣṭho vā pañca yajñān samāhitaḥ /
kuryādaharahaḥ snātvā bhikṣānnenaiva tena hi //
2.28.d:
वेदान्तज्ञाननिष्ठो वा पञ्च यज्ञान् समाहितः ।
कुर्यादहरहः स्नात्वा भिक्षान्नेनैव तेन हि ॥
2.28.m: Or, devoted to the knowledge of the Vedānta, composed in mind, / having bathed day after day, he should perform the five sacrifices indeed with begged food.

2.28.s:
homamantrāñjapennityaṃ kāle kāle samāhitaḥ /
svādhyāyaṃ cānvahaṃ kuryāt sāvitrīṃ saṃdhyayorjapet //
2.28.d:
होममन्त्राञ्जपेन्नित्यं काले काले समाहितः ।
स्वाध्यायं चान्वहं कुर्यात् सावित्रीं संध्ययोर्जपेत् ॥
2.28.m: He should constantly murmur the fire-offering mantras at the proper times, composed; / he should perform daily recitation of the Veda every day, and murmur the Sāvitrī verse at both twilights.

2.28.s:
dhyāyīta satataṃ devamekānte parameśvaram /
ekānnaṃ varjayennityaṃ kāmaṃ krodhaṃ parigraham //
2.28.d:
ध्यायीत सततं देवमेकान्ते परमेश्वरम् ।
एकान्नं वर्जयेन्नित्यं कामं क्रोधं परिग्रहम् ॥
2.28.m: He should constantly meditate in solitude on the god, the Supreme Lord; / he should always avoid food from a single source, lust, anger, and possessions.

2.28.s:
ekavāsā dvivāsā vā śikhī yajñopavītavān /
kamaṇḍalukaro vidvān tridaṇḍī yāti tatparam //
iti śrīkūrmapurāṇe ṣaṭsāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāmuparivibhāge 'ṣṭāviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.28.d:
एकवासा द्विवासा वा शिखी यज्ञोपवीतवान् ।
कमण्डलुकरो विद्वान् त्रिदण्डी याति तत्परम् ॥
इति श्रीकूर्मपुराणे षट्साहस्त्र्यां संहितायामुपरिविभागे ऽष्टाविंशो ऽध्यायः
2.28.m:
Wearing one garment or two garments, wearing a tuft of hair and a sacred thread, / carrying a water pot in hand, wise, carrying three staffs, he attains that supreme state.

Thus ends the twenty-eighth chapter in the latter section of the compilation consisting of six thousand verses in the glorious Kūrma Purāṇa.
